final.headline: The strongest use of this footage is the real Tokyo roast day, shown at native speed: the drum drop into the cooling-tray loop as the Story page's one dark band, the four SNöBI bags arriving one by one in window sun as the /coffee header, and the real bag in daylight right after the 3D bag on each origin page. The same clips also give the 10 s spot drop-in upgrades and one 'green, then brown' Reel.
footage_truths: Everything is one Tokyo morning: roastery bench, roaster, café bar, outdoor brew table. There is no farm or origin footage, so captions must say Tokyo. The 4K 3840x2160 originals and the 2026-10-01 shoot date are reported VERIFIED in grade/README.md by the concept authors; I did not re-open it.

Only seven clips show SNöBI bags: 6586 (four-bag table), 6572 (Ethiopia opened on the sunlit desk), 7111 (four bags behind the mug pour), 7074 (Mexico decaf pouch beside the pour-over), and 7199/7208/7209 (Peru in hand against dark sacks). In 7669 the bag being SNöBI is INFERRED: the name is never legible and the label is upside-down. 7695 is VERIFIED as an 'ode by TOKYO COFFEE' bag and must not be used for SNöBI.

Labels are a liability. Every back label prints 焙煎日 2026/09/22 and will look stale on the site. On the 7208 Peru label the table values sit one row below their headers and the barcode reads 0000000000000 (VERIFIED). The same print on 7199/7209 is INFERRED. The 6572 Ethiopia label is UNKNOWN. Use front labels only until a full-resolution check is done.

Falling beans cannot be slowed. Optical-flow 50% ghosts the streaks (VERIFIED with ffmpeg minterpolate on 7236 and 7251), so every cascade (7703 drop, 7289 green, 7266/7251 plate) runs at 100%. The 50% treatment suits static or slow subjects: 6586 bag beats, 7111 mug pour, 7052 bloom, 7209 bean hold, 7703 tray arm (warp check needed).

9:16 almost never holds a bag or a group: bags are 0.30-0.56 of frame width against a 0.316 window. Clean verticals exist only for central falling columns and texture: 7289 at 0.55, 7703 drop at 0.52, 7266 at 0.50, 7251 at 0.49, 7052 bloom at 0.48, 7703 tray at 0.66, and single-bag 6586 Peru at 0.37 (zero margin). Bag shots work as 16:9, 4:5 or 1:1.

Verified clean loops: 6586 19.02-22.22 (once stabilised with roll correction, aligned diff 3.0); 7703 53.6-57.3 (one tray-arm revolution); 7703 4.1-5.3 (window tumble); 7209 16.05-17.65 (beans, diff 8.22); 6572 1.17-2.07 (ping-pong only); 7596 0.2-3.2 and 12.81-15.82; 7289 7.4-9.4 with crossfade; 6788 34.03-38.44 (espresso, not SNöBI).

Light: the daylight sets are 6586, 6572, 7111, 7074, 7052 and the 7236-7273 plates (luma about 110-145). The dark material is the 7703 tray (L about 34), 7596 drum (about 56), 7703 chute (about 57-73), and the 7199/7208/7209 green-sack background (75-107). That allows one dark band on the whole site, and the roast is the right one.

The café clips 6786, 6787, 6788, 6789, 6790 and 6791 show no SNöBI bag and are dominated by third-party brands: La Marzocco, Torani, OCD, Bomber, HARIO on 7052/7074 after about 8 s and 13.8 s. The venue is INFERRED. These clips stay off SNöBI commerce pages.

measure_film's shot counts are wrong on 6786, 6788, 6789, 6790, 7266, 7289, 7695 and 7703: every clip is a single take, and the false cuts are camera moves. In particular 7703 is one continuous take, so you can cut the drop sequence on the camera's own moves.

The plate set 7236/7244/7251/7266/7273 is styled and brand-neutral and could belong to any roaster. The settled piles in 7236 and 7244 contain visible quakers and shells, so close stills need retouching. Use it only as motion in a sequence that already carries the brand.

ranked.name: Story: the drop (the site's one dark band)
ranked.surface: /about Story section: a full-width dark band with copy on the left and a 4:5 film panel on the right. A 9:16 Reel cut of the drop alone comes from the same render.
ranked.what_viewer_sees: Copy reads 東京で焙煎。火曜・金曜に焼いて、翌営業日に発送。 The film runs: 0-2.4 s roasted beans glow and tumble behind the chute window (slowed). Dissolve. 2.4-4.6 s frontal chute: the operator's hand swings the drop door open and a wall of beans breaks over the steel. 4.6-6.6 s hands gone, the full cascade pours into the cooling tray on a locked camera. 6.6-8.6 s the stream thins to the last beans. Dissolve down. 8.6-12.3 s the black stirring arm sweeps one revolution through the fresh bed, and that revolution loops for as long as the band is on screen. Scroll past and the page is paper again. Reduced motion shows a poster at 32.2.

clips.treatment: 50% optical flow gives 2.4 s. Hand-free and steady (jerk 0.195), and the verified 4.1-5.3 loop window. A 4:5 crop at about 0.45 drops the kitchen timer and card at the right edge. Out before the fingers enter at 5.5.

100%; interpolation would warp the fingers and the first wall of beans. Stabilise (0.8-2 px/frame handheld) so it joins the locked section. 4:5 crop at 0.55. Door opens at 29.86 (VERIFIED luma 79 to 43).
100%. Camera effectively locked (0.55-0.82 px/frame); the 0.294 jerk comes from the beans. 4:5 crop at 0.52 removes the timer. Hands clear from 32.2.
100%, locked (jerk 0.16). 4:5 crop at 0.50. Out before the chute runs empty at about 37.7.

100% by default (thin arm edges over bean texture are a warp risk); try 50% if a RIFE test passes. Stabilise the nudge at 54.0. 4:5 crop at about 0.66. Seamless one-revolution loop with a 6-8 frame crossfade (diff 12.42, endpoints compared). Grade the whole band as one piece; tray lift of about +0.35 stop from L 34.

ranked.why: No other brand can show this: our drum dropping a batch in Tokyo, cut only on the camera's own moves inside one continuous take, so it reads as one event. It puts the site's single permitted dark moment exactly where the copy says 焙煎. It ends on the only truly endless mechanical motion in the shoot (the tray revolution), so it also replaces the standalone 'One revolution' Reel. Every in and out point is VERIFIED in the inventory.
ranked.risks: There is a big luma step from the chute (about 57-73) to the tray (about 34), so grade the band together. The kitchen timer and card must be out of every chute crop, which is why the panel is 4:5. The smartwatch and ring show on the door shot (consent covered, no readable brand). The /about page is a later site-plan phase. Home (rank 3) quotes 1.8 s of the same cascade, which is intentional and works like a trailer.
ranked.scores: J1 impact 8 / brand fit 9 / footage 8 / feasibility 8 (do); J2 8/9/8/7 (do). Merged with 'One-take The drop' (J1 7/9/8/8, J2 7/9/9/8), which survives as the 9:16 Reel cut (7703 32.2-37.5 at crop 0.52, 100%) and the fallback.

ranked.name: /coffee header: the four arrive
ranked.surface: /coffee header: a full-width 16:9 band (max about 56vh) above the comparison of the four coffees. Mobile keeps 16:9 because no portrait crop holds the group.
ranked.what_viewer_sees: 0-2.0 s: the empty oak table in hard window sun with a plant-shaped shadow; the page title sits in the shaded wood at upper left. Dissolve: the Peru bag appears in the sunlit patch, and no hand is ever seen. Dissolve: Mexico (DECAF) stands beside it. Dissolve: Ethiopia behind. Dissolve: Colombia completes the group in front, and the frame settles into a breathing loop with a crossfaded seam while the band is in view. The comparison columns below follow the arrival order. Cards carry stills, not hover video.

clips.treatment: 50% gives 2.0 s. Stabilise and align to the shared build frame: about 65-70 px offset at the same scale, with roll correction. Clean-plate patch over the specks at x 0.34-0.46, y 0.24-0.40 on every frame. Grade-match up to the Peru beat: this plate sits at luma 101-109, the Peru beat at 124-136.
50% gives 1.6 s. Lock to the shared frame. The smoothest second of the clip (jerk 0.089). No hand: the fingertip has gone by 9.65 and the next bag enters at 11.25.
50% gives 1.8 s. Hand-free beat (12.25-13.5). Align: about 1.7 deg and 85 px from the Peru beat.
50% gives 1.4 s. Hand-free beat (14.9-15.7). Ethiopia reads only 'ETHI' here.

100% (static). Stabilise to locked with about 3 deg of roll correction, then loop with a short crossfade (aligned diff 3.0 vs 14.6 raw). Crop in roughly 10-20% from the 4K original (INFERRED estimate). Poster at 20.8.

ranked.why: This is the approved 3D 'four bags line up' idea done with real bags in real sun, with the placing hands edited out. A page whose job is choosing between four coffees opens by assembling them, and nothing dated is printed in frame, so it never goes stale. It merges 'The lineup builds' (same windows, minus the empty-table opening) and beats the 'One-take Four arrive' version, which keeps blurred real-speed hands.
ranked.risks: Roll and drift between beats run up to about 6.5 deg and 100 px. Any misalignment makes the plant shadow 'swim' through the dissolves, so align on the table, which is fixed to the shadow. In the final hold Peru shows only 'P' and Ethiopia 'ETHIO', so the cards below must name them. The median shot is about 1.6 s, at the bottom of the band. Half the table is in deep shade, so trim the concrete at top left. Fallback if alignment fails: the one-take 6586 9.7-22.42 at real speed.
ranked.scores: J1 7/8/7/6 (do); J2 7/9/7/5 (do). Absorbs 'The lineup builds' (J1 6/8/7/6 maybe, J2 7/9/7/6 maybe).

ranked.name: Home hero: an empty cup to a full one (real footage replaces the Ken Burns stills)
ranked.surface: Home hero, in the same slot as the 22 s still-photo film in components/lab/film-hero.tsx: a 3:2 framed film on paper with the cart always visible. The same 3:2 file runs full-width on phones.
ranked.what_viewer_sees: 0-2.2 s: four SNöBI bags in low side sun behind an empty glass mug, with MEXICO DECAF, COLOMBIA huila and ETHIOPIA guji readable. オーガニックのまま、スペシャルティ。 sits on the bare wood left of the mug. Dissolve. About 1.8 s of the drum door already open, a wall of fresh roast pouring into the cooling tray (the only dark beat), with 東京で焙煎。火曜・金曜に焼いて、 Dissolve. 2.0 s looking down into the opened Ethiopia bag, glossy beans, in striped desk sun. Dissolve. 5.0 s back at the first table: a golden stream falls into the same mug with the Ethiopia bag sharp behind, and the mug fills. It freezes on the half-full mug with no hands as the poster. まずは、一杯から。 and the 4種を見る button settle under it. No replay. Reduced motion and Save-Data show the poster only.

clips.treatment: 50% gives 2.2 s, inside the steady 4-9 s window (jerk 0.156). Stabilise locked to the bags. 3:2 window anchored right (x 0.156-1.0, 1620 px native) drops the server sliver. Patch the white specks left of the mug.

100% (streak ghosting). The camera is locked and the timer is static, so clone the kitchen timer out instead of relying on the crop: a left-anchored 3:2 at 1.02x ends at about x 0.827 against the timer at 0.83, which is zero margin.

Replaces the generic 7237 plate shot, which both judges flagged as brand-neutral. 50% gives 2.0 s (steady stretch, jerk 0.169). Punch in about 1.2x anchored upper-left from the 4K original to push the smartwatch face at lower right out of frame; check frame 20.5. Out before the hand switch at 22.2.

50% gives 5.0 s. In at 19.0 instead of 18.8 to clear the fingers, which leave at about 18.8. Same right-anchored 3:2 as shot 1. Check every interpolated frame where the stream crosses the Colombia and centre-back label text. Freeze 21.5 as the poster.

ranked.why: The whole promise fits on one table: the bags and an empty cup, the real Tokyo drop, beans in the opened bag, then the same cup full. Every frame is ours (SNöBI labels, our roaster). It lasts about 10 s instead of 22 s and ends on a still, so Home is calm before the release cards. It answers the brief's core ask of real footage replacing the stills.
ranked.risks: It fills the same slot as the Ken Burns film, so it does not require retiring the approved 3D scroll scene. If Home then reads as having two signatures, the owner chooses; the fallback is a single still at 7111 19.5. Envelope: 4 shots in about 10 s (2.2 / 1.8 / 2.0 / 5.0 minus three 10-frame dissolves), open 2.2, close 5.0, median about 2.0. The drop runs at 100% between 50% shots, so the speed change will be felt; keep the dissolves long. Peru is hidden in the lineup (only 'PE' shows), on the most important frame of the site. Byte estimate about 3.5 MB at 1620x1080 (INFERRED).
ranked.scores: J1 7/7/7/5 (maybe; asked to cut the 7237 plate insert, now done); J2 8/8/8/6 (do; decouple from retiring the 3D scene, now done).

ranked.name: 10 s spot: real footage in beats 1, 4 and 5 (a proposal to the video session)
ranked.surface: The 10 s Instagram spot, 9:16 1080x1920. Beats, frames and strings stay exactly as storyboard v0. This is offered to the session that owns the spot, not a storyboard change.
ranked.what_viewer_sees: Beat 1 (0-1.0 s): the Peru bag alone on sunlit oak, full-bleed 9:16, PERU readable within 15 frames, with the sun-shaft wipe. Beat 2 (spot owner's call): either the approved 'three bags slide in', or a framed 16:9 footage plate of all four bags on the same table. Beat 3: unchanged label-macro still. Beat 4 (5.0-7.0 s): overhead pour-over, water spreading over dry grounds, the first CO2 bubbles at about 6.2-6.6. Beat 5 (7.0-8.5 s): hands holding a Peru bag open, beans sharp in the mouth. Beat 6: the end card as approved.

clips.treatment: 50% gives 1.0 s. 9:16 crop at x 0.37 from the 4K original; valid only for source 10.2-11.0. The bag is 0.30 wide in a 0.316 window, so the 28 px rise needs about 1.03 overscan or must be dropped (spot owner decides).
Optional beat-2 plate. 50% gives 2.0 s, stabilised (26 px drift). Framed 16:9 on paper. All four names are readable here, the only time they are together.

50% gives 2.0 s. 9:16 crop at x 0.48 from 4K excludes the kettle bar. Check the stream and bubbles frame by frame; fallback is 100% over 2.4-4.4. The coffee is UNKNOWN, so no on-screen claim goes over it.
50% gives 1.5 s. 9:16 crop at x 0.55 from 4K, inside the sharp bean hold. Lift about +0.3 stop against the dark sacks.

ranked.why: The footage comes from the same session as the stills the storyboard already uses. Swapping each still for its moving twin keeps the approved compositions and adds real life: sun on the bag, CO2 bubbles, beans in hands. Every crop is inventory-listed and cut from 4K, with no proxy upscale. The concept also caught three errors in the current v3/v02: its shot 1 (7074 @15.0) sits inside the unusable 12.5-16.3 push-in, its shot 2 (7703 @31.0) still has the hand on the handle until about 31.9, and its shot 5 measured jerk 0.251. Better in-points are 7074 17.4-20.9 and 7703 from 32.2.
ranked.risks: The video session owns the storyboard, so this must stay a proposal; beat 2 is its call. The beat-1 crop has zero margin. Beat 5's background is dark green sacks inside a paper world; the alternate is 6572 20.0-20.75 (crop 0.53, an Ethiopia bag, watch risk). 'Light roast.' over 7052 makes no claim about which coffee is brewing.

ranked.name: Origin pages: the real bag right after the 3D bag (with a live roast date on the 3D stamp)
ranked.surface: /origins/peru, /mexico, /ethiopia and /colombia: one clip directly after the drag-to-rotate 3D bag and before facts and the buy card. A shared media governor pauses the 3D render loop while the clip plays, and the reverse, so only one thing moves per viewport.
ranked.what_viewer_sees: The visitor spins the 3D bag; its back face now lands on a roast-date stamp computed from the registry (for example 次の焙煎 10/9（金）). Below it, captioned 同じ袋を、窓の光で。／東京で撮影: Ethiopia (4:5), held up in hard striped desk sun, barely breathing on a seamless 3.6 s cycle. Peru (4:5), alone on the oak table in window sun, settling over 1.6 s and resting on its sharpest frame. Colombia (4:5), front-centre of the four on the same table, label fully readable, neighbours soft at the edges, breathing loop. Mexico (16:9), the only origin with its own brew footage: a wide gooseneck pour beside the MEXICO honey chiapas DECAF pouch in low hard sun, dissolving to a sharp close on the stream into the foam pool, then back.

clips.treatment: Ethiopia. Stabilise (raw jerk 0.287). 50% gives 1.8 s, played forward then reversed (3.6 s); this is the only clean loop of that bag. 4:5 crop centred 0.45 (about 0.025 margin a side). Check the green watch band at lower right. Poster 1.5.
Peru. 50% gives 1.6 s, played once and resting on the poster at 10.5. 4:5 crop centred 0.37 (valid for 10.2-11.0), stabilised with roll correction. Front label only.
Colombia. Stabilised to locked with roll correction, 100% loop with a crossfaded seam (the same render as the /coffee loop). 4:5 crop centred 0.51.

Mexico wide. 50% gives 2.5 s. Near-locked camera (0.02-0.13 px/frame). 16:9 only (4:5 loses the pouch). Fingertips sit at the top-left edge until about 12.2: punch in about 1.05-1.08x anchored bottom-right (the amount is INFERRED; measure it). Check the thin stream for warps.

Mexico close. Stabilise the 0.3-1.5 px/frame wander, then 50% gives 2.6 s, inside the sharp window 17.4-20.9. The HARIO 'ARIO' collar must be masked or retouched. 10-frame dissolves loop back to the wide.

ranked.why: The 3D bag is the promise and the film is the receipt: the same pouch in real light before the buyer reaches the price. This answers the 'other photos of each bag' question in motion. Moving the live roast date onto the 3D stamp means the footage never has to show a dated label. It merges the 'Tokyo coda' (date stamp, honest Tokyo caption) and 'Decaf in the low sun' (the Mexico slot with its own bag in frame), so each page has one slot instead of two.
ranked.risks: Colombia comes from the shared four-bag frame; a 10-minute single-bag reshoot per origin in the same sun would fix it (see gaps). The 3D model's label art must match the real pouch, or the cut exposes it. The 4:5 crops from the proxy are 864 px wide, so use the 4K originals. Mexico continuity: the server is already about a third full before the pour; it barely reads in 2.5 s. The 'late in the day' framing is INFERRED from the sun, so the copy asserts no time. The roast-date stamp needs the registry's roast days and cutoff first; it must be computed, never typed.
ranked.scores: Same sun: J1 6/8/6/6 (maybe), J2 6/8/7/7 (do). Coda: J1 5/8/6/7, J2 5/8/6/7 (maybe). Decaf pair: J1 6/8/7/7 (do), J2 5/7/7/7 (maybe).

ranked.name: Reel 'Green, then brown' (three falls)
ranked.surface: Instagram Reel, 9:16, about 9.5 s after dissolve overlap
ranked.what_viewer_sees: Grey-green beans fall as a curtain onto a growing mound. Then green beans tumble behind the roaster's sight window, the one dark beat. Then the drop: brown beans pour over the stainless chute on a locked camera. Then roasted beans rain onto a pale plate and split the cluster into two lobes. It ends on the plate at rest; オーガニックのまま、スペシャルティ。 and snobi.jp appear in the top third over plain bean texture. Each dissolve is a match on a falling column held near the centre of the crop.

clips.treatment: 100%, stabilised, with a 3-frame blend. 9:16 crop at 0.55 from 4K excludes the blue bin corner that returns at 7.2. Warm the grey-beige beans.
100% plus blend (baked-in streaks). Out at 14.9, before the vertical ease-back. Stabilised to locked. 9:16 crop at 0.53; hinge symmetry is lost.
100% plus blend. Locked camera, hands clear from 32.2. 9:16 crop at 0.52 excludes the timer.
100%. Light stabilise (about 2 px/frame). 9:16 crop at 0.50 keeps the stream (x 0.48-0.53) and the impact. Peak 9.1-9.4, split 9.8.
100%, near-locked (under 1% drift). 9:16 crop at 0.50. Type sits in the top third on bean texture.

ranked.why: One idea only a roaster can post: the same gesture at three moments in a bean's life. Every crop holds its subject, because each fall is a central column, the one shot type that survives 9:16 in this footage. It reads with the sound off and costs little.
ranked.risks: At 100% it feels faster than the site's slowed films; one 50% test of shots 1 and 4 is worth doing. The green and roasted beans are not provably the same lot, so nothing on screen claims they are. The 7266 stream is a translucent streak, so the impact reads better than the fall. Needs a licensed music track.

ranked.name: Brand film 'One table, three falls' (tightened to about 25 s)
ranked.surface: Story page header (click-to-play, sound on) and YouTube 1920x1080, conformed from the 4K originals.
ranked.what_viewer_sees: An empty oak table in late-morning sun. The Peru bag appears through an aligned dissolve. Green beans fall as a curtain. A short dark passage: green beans tumble behind the sight window, the batch drops over the chute, the tray arm sweeps. Back to light: a sealed bag slides out of the band sealer onto the teal belt, with 火曜と金曜に焙煎。焙煎日は袋に。 on the empty belt. The oak table again with Peru and Mexico. The Ethiopia bag held up in striped sun, then looking down into its opened mouth. Water meets dry grounds and CO2 erupts. The table with three bags. A golden stream into a glass mug with the Ethiopia bag behind. All four bags held, the wordmark and オーガニックのまま、スペシャルティ。 in the shaded wood. The last frame is the poster.

clips.treatment: 50% gives 2.6 s. Locked and aligned to shot 2. Patch the specks. Fade in from warm tone.
50% gives 2.0 s. Aligned so table and shadow stay put through the dissolve.
50% gives 1.8 s (blue corner absent from 3.6 to 6.9). Fallback: 100% over 5.6-7.4 with a blend if it ghosts.
100% plus 3-frame blend, giving 1.4 s. Out before the ease-back at 14.9. 1.5x punch-in on the window from 4K.
100% (the v02 sibling measured 0.22 after the 50% chain), giving 1.8 s. Clone out the timer.
50% gives 2.2 s. Stabilise the nudge at 54.0. +0.35 stop.
50% gives 2.4 s, light stabilise. Conditional on the owner confirming the bag is SNöBI; otherwise cut it. Type on the lower-left belt only (the label is upside-down).
50% gives 1.8 s. Roll and drift aligned to shot 2.
50% gives 1.8 s. Stabilised. 1.15x punch-in anchored left drops the watch band and trouser edge.
50% gives 2.0 s. About 1.2x punch-in anchored upper-left to remove the smartwatch; check 20.5.
Fixed in-point: the original 2.3 missed first contact at 2.07-2.14. 50% gives 2.0 s. 1.15x punch-in anchored right drops the kettle bar. Frame-by-frame warp check.
50% gives 1.2 s (hand-free 14.9-15.7). Aligned.
50% gives 2.4 s, no hands, jerk 0.153.
50% gives 3.6 s. Locked with about 3 deg roll correction. Type in the shaded wood. Fade out; the last frame is the poster.

ranked.why: This is the most ambitious honest film the footage can make: one Tokyo morning with no farm and no stock. Two wordless devices carry it. The oak table returns four times and gains a bag each time, and everything in between falls (green beans, the drop, water, coffee). Tightened from 33.8 s: the styled 7244 plate shot and the 7074 wide pour are cut, the bloom in-point is fixed to show first contact, and the dissolve overlap is now counted. That gives 14 shots in about 24.7 s, 5.7 per 10 s, median 2.0, open 2.6, close 3.6.
ranked.risks: The dark roast passage is three consecutive shots (about 5.4 s); reading that as 'one dark moment' needs the owner's OK. If the 7669 bag is not SNöBI, cut the sealer shot. Several falling-bean shots may fall back to 100%. The table returns need up to about 6.5 deg and 100 px of alignment. smooth_shot.sh is proven only on proxies. The renderer needs brand fonts (whether the Adobe Dynamic kit loads is UNKNOWN; otherwise use the wordmark SVG). Needs licensed music at about 120 BPM. Do it after the site pieces.
ranked.scores: J1 8/8/7/5 (do; tighten to about 25 s and drop the plate shot, now done); J2 8/8/7/4 (maybe; dissolve overlap and the bloom in-point, both fixed).

ranked.name: Trade: the range at the counter, then the chain behind it
ranked.surface: /trade: a 16:9 hero (1:1 on mobile) above a static three-tile row headed 仕入れの流れ. One tile moves; the other two are stills. Each tile carries one fact line from the registry.
ranked.what_viewer_sees: Hero: four SNöBI bags on a wood table in low side sun; in front of them a glass server pours an amber stream into a glass mug, and it comes to rest on the half-full mug. Tiles: 生豆, a still of green coffee falling onto a mound. 焙煎, a 2.4 s loop of beans tumbling behind the roaster window. 封緘, a still of a sealed bag on the teal belt (only if the bag is confirmed as SNöBI). Fact lines: 火・金焙煎 / 焙煎日翌営業日発送 / 100g・200g, plus wholesale size, MOQ and lead time once the owner supplies them.

clips.treatment: 50% gives 5.4 s. Hands-free, jerk 0.153. Plays once and rests on 21.5. Desktop 16:9; mobile 1:1 centred 0.67 (mug, stream, full Ethiopia label, handle cut). Type on the lower-left wood only.

Still for the 生豆 tile from the 3.6-6.9 window, where the blue bin corner is absent. A 1:1 crop at 0.55 is not verified for the corner at other times. Warm the grade. Caption 生豆, never 有機生豆 (lot unverified).
The one moving tile. 50% gives 2.4 s, seamless loop (diff 9.39), hand-free. 1:1 crop centred 0.45 drops the timer and card.
Still for the 封緘 tile, conditional on confirming the bag as SNöBI. The 1:1 crop at about 0.55 must be measured to hold the bag, tail and pulley.

ranked.why: Café buyers want reliability. The hero shows the whole range at the counter in one frame, and the tiles show the real chain behind it (green, roast, seal) on real machines. It replaces the dropped espresso-stream concept, which showed no SNöBI identity. Making two of the three tiles stills keeps the page to one signature move.
ranked.risks: The 7669 bag identity is INFERRED; never use 7695 (a VERIFIED 'ode' bag). Which coffee is in the hero server is UNKNOWN, so the page claims nothing about it. Wholesale terms are UNKNOWN until the owner supplies them; roast days and the ship rule must read the same registry entries as the cart.
ranked.scores: J1 6/7/7/5 (maybe; asked for stills in the tiles, now done); J2 6/7/7/6 (do).

ranked.name: Journal: the first Roastery post, green to sealed
ranked.surface: /journal/[slug], Roastery category: an MDX post with muted video <Figure> loops (a poster until in view, one playing at a time). The cover still is 7290 at 22.
ranked.what_viewer_sees: A long-form post. Fig. 1 (9:16): green coffee rains onto a growing mound beside JAS有機認証の豆だけを。 (wording for the owner; the lot is unverified). Fig. 2 (9:16): the settled green pile from directly overhead. Fig. 3: olive beans tumbling behind the drum window, early in the roast. Fig. 4 (9:16): the cooling-tray arm sweeping a fresh batch. Fig. 5 (16:9, only if the bag is confirmed): a sealed bag slides out of the band sealer, beside 翌営業日に発送。

ranked.why: The Journal is the honest home for true footage that is too long, dim or specialised for commerce pages: the green coffee, the drum, the tray and the sealer. It costs little once the Journal exists, and dim figures are acceptable inside an editorial.
ranked.risks: Fig. 5 depends on the 7669 confirmation, and four figures is enough. The green beans read grey-beige and the blue bin needs grading. The Journal <Figure> needs a video variant. About 5-6 MB if a reader scrolls the whole post (INFERRED). Later phase (site-plan §3).

ranked.name: 焙煎日は袋に: label proof next to the buy card (gated on a label fix)
ranked.surface: /origins/[slug] module under the buy card, plus an optional still chip on ProductCard. Ship only after the label passes a full-resolution check, or after a reshoot.
ranked.what_viewer_sees: A bag held toward the lens, the info label facing us. It freezes, and a thin plum SVG ring draws around the printed 焙煎日 line, captioned 見本：2026年9月22日（火）焙煎の袋. Beside it, a line computed from the registry: 火曜と金曜に焙煎。次の焙煎 10月9日（金）→ 発送 …. A 10-frame dissolve leads to the same bag open, whole beans with pale centre cuts, looping every 3.2 s under 豆のまま。挽くのは淹れる直前に。

clips.treatment: Real speed (fingers and text warp under interpolation). Fixes the timeline contradiction: play 1.0-2.8 and freeze on the last frame (2.8, inside the sharpest window 2.5-3.2) instead of running to 3.5 and jumping back. 4:5 crop at 0.55, keyframed for the label's drift from x 0.48 to 0.58.
50% gives 3.2 s. Seamless loop with a 0.4 s crossfade (diff 8.22, beans sharp throughout). Check the nail and bag-rim edges for warps.

ranked.why: Both judges liked the idea: a printed specimen next to a live computed date turns 焙煎日は袋に into something the buyer can plan around without claiming roasted-to-order. It merges 'Read the bag' (the four-claim callouts on the 6572 Ethiopia label) into one module so the site does not carry two label-proof pieces. The callouts can return on a reshot clean label.
ranked.risks: STOP condition. The 7208 Peru label (same lot) is VERIFIED misregistered with a zero barcode; 7209 is INFERRED to carry the same print; the 6572 label is UNKNOWN. Check full-resolution frames of 7209 (2.8) and 6572 (4.0, 4.5, 10.0) first. If either fails, fix the template, reprint, and reshoot one bag on the 6572 desk in daylight; that also fixes the dark-sack background (luma 75-107) and the problem of one Peru take appearing on all four pages. This may be a food-labelling issue beyond the website. The ship date must come from one function reading the roast days, cutoff (UNKNOWN), JP holidays and business days. Until then show only the existing cart line 火・金焙煎。焙煎日翌営業日に発送。
ranked.scores: 焙煎日は袋に: J1 7/7/5/4 (maybe), J2 7/6/5/4 (maybe). Read the bag: J1 6/7/5/4 (maybe), J2 6/5/4/4 (drop).

hero_shortlist.why: The drop with hands clear: a dense wall of fresh roast pours over the chute into the tray on a locked camera. The single most ownable event in the shoot, and it crops cleanly at 9:16 0.52.
One full revolution of the cooling-tray arm with jerk 0.065: a verified seamless loop and the site's dark band in a single shot.
All four SNöBI bags in hard window sun. Once stabilised it loops seamlessly (aligned diff 3.0). This is the end frame for /coffee and the brand film.
Peru alone on sunlit oak, the smoothest second of the shoot (jerk 0.089), the brightest frame, no hands. It also gives a single-bag 9:16 crop at 0.37.
A hands-free golden stream into a glass mug with the Ethiopia guji label sharp behind and the other bags in frame. It is the product-to-cup payoff in one steady shot (jerk 0.153).
The Ethiopia Guji front label held still in striped desk sun with other bags soft behind. The cleanest hand-held bag hero, and it ping-pongs seamlessly.
Whole beans in the opened Peru bag, sharp throughout. The best loop in the shoot (diff 8.22) and a strong 9:16 at 0.55.
First water touches dry grounds at about 2.1 and CO2 erupts at about 3.2. The cleanest naturally slow subject (jerk max 0.168), with no hands and no third-party marks inside this window.
A near-locked wide pour-over in low hard sun beside the MEXICO honey chiapas DECAF pouch, label readable. The only brew shot with its own bag in frame.
A green-coffee cascade onto a built mound. A crossfade loop that crops clean at 9:16 0.55 and opens the green-to-brown story.

dropped: Trade: espresso stream beside the inquiry (6788 34.03-38.44). Both judges dropped it as a generic espresso shot with no SNöBI identity; venue and beans are unproven. The loop also starts inside the 33.7-34.8 sway. Replaced by rank 8.

Cart: drum window next to the roast-day line (7596 0.2-3.2). Both judges dropped it: at about 160 px the motion-streaked olive beans read as murky raw coffee, and it puts motion at checkout. Keep only the registry fix (derive the cart line and nextRoastDay() from one source).

The plate fills to free shipping (7251 3.0-12.4). A gimmick on the brand-neutral plate set, with the darker plate as the 'success' state; 3.0-3.83 has jerk above 0.40. Keep only the fix that moves the ¥3,000 threshold into the registry.
Reel 'First water' (7052 bloom one-take). J1 dropped it as a generic bloom every account posts; J2 rated it do. The bloom lives on inside the brand film and beat 4 of the spot instead.
Reel 'One revolution' (7703 53.6-57.3) as a standalone post. A fully dark reel breaks the light-world rule; the loop is used as the end of the Story drop band (rank 1).
One-take 'Four arrive' (6586 9.7-22.42). Both judges dropped it: blurred real-speed hand placements and arm-shadow dips. Kept only as the fallback if the dissolve alignment in rank 2 fails.
The lineup builds. Merged into rank 2 (same 6586 windows).
One-take 'The drop'. Merged into rank 1 as the 9:16 Reel cut and fallback.
Origin coda 'after it reaches Tokyo' and 'Decaf in the low sun'. Merged into rank 5 (live roast-date stamp, Tokyo caption, and the Mexico brew pair as the Mexico slot).
Read the bag: four claims (6572 8.55-10.0). Merged into rank 10. The moving part is a 1.45 s shaky tear (jerk 0.342) on the bright luma swing, over an unverified label.
FAQ bloom in the roast-date answer (7052 2.0-7.9). Both judges rated it a low-impact maybe: a generic image with the coffee UNKNOWN. Deferred; the asset is reused in the film and spot.

Reel 'Open a Peru' (7209 3.9-17.65). Deferred: dark green-sack background, a weak 12.8-13.8 reveal, shot 1 at 50% against the inventory's native-only advice, and it sits next to a probably misregistered label. Revisit after the label fix and a daylight reshoot.
Home hero's 7237 plate insert (0.6-1.3). Removed as brand-neutral styled footage; replaced by 6572 19.9-20.9 looking into the opened bag.
Brand film shots 7244 10.0-11.0 (plate heart) and 7074 10.25-11.45 (wide pour). Cut to tighten the film to about 25 s and drop styled plate footage.

Never use for SNöBI: 7695 (VERIFIED 'ode by TOKYO COFFEE' bag), 6786 and 6787 (Torani and La Marzocco, dark bar), 6790 and 6791 (café latte, Torani), 6789 (café barista, not the roaster), 7208 (label table misregistered, zero barcode), 7236 (quakers in the settled pile, accidental whip), and 7052 after 8 s and 7074 after 13.8 s (HARIO).
gaps: Each origin bag alone on the 6586 oak table and the 6572 desk in the same hard sun, on a tripod, hand-free, 10 s locked per bag (Ethiopia, Mexico, Colombia especially). This ends the recentred-crop compromise on the origin pages and gives a clean 'other photo of each bag' in motion.
A corrected, reprinted label (table aligned, real barcode) shot front and back in daylight on a tripod, plus a tight insert of the 焙煎日 line. Rank 10 is blocked until this exists.
The roast-date stamp being applied, and bags being filled and weighed: the action behind 焙煎日は袋に, which no clip currently shows.

The drop and the cooling tray on a locked tripod at 60-120p with a faster shutter, so the cascades can be slowed in-camera without interpolation ghosting, and without the kitchen timer on the tray rim.
A daylight establishing shot of the roastery: the room and window light, the roaster wide. Every current roaster frame is a dark close-up.
Green coffee with its organic lot identifiable (JAS-marked sack or tag in frame), so a green-bean shot can carry 有機 honestly.
Pour-over or brewing of Peru, Ethiopia and Colombia with each bag in frame, and a dripper without a third-party wordmark. Only Mexico has brew footage today.
The band sealer with a SNöBI bag fed label-up and its name legible, so the seal beat can carry the brand (the 7669 bag is upside-down and unconfirmed).
Packing and dispatch: box, shipping label, hand-off. This supports 翌営業日発送 and gives the Trade page a final link.
Native 9:16 verticals of the bag lineup and a single bag, shot vertically, since no horizontal group shot survives a 9:16 crop.

inventory.summary: One continuous handheld take, 32.6 s with no cuts, of hands opening a 100 g SNöBI Ethiopia Guji bag over a wooden desk in hard, striped sunlight. In order: front label, back label, tear strip and zip, a look into the beans, a short tip of beans into the palm (about 0.5 s), then the bag set on the desk and pressed shut as the camera pulls back to show PERU, MEXICO (decaf) and other SNöBI bags. Hands only, no faces, warm and light (look_v3). Only two stretches pass the jerk rule: 19.7-22.15 s (beans in the open bag) and 29.4-31.7 s (desk outro). The rest is hand action with per-second jerk up to 0.53.

inventory.verify_notes:
Method: I extracted and read frames at 0.0, 0.2, 1.2, 1.5, 2.5, 2.8, 3.0, 3.2, 3.4, 4.5, 6.0, 8.3, 8.55, 8.8, 9.2, 10.0, 12.0, 14.8, 15.2, 15.6, 17.65, 18.4, 19.0, 19.5, 20.5, 21.6, 22.1, 22.4, 22.8, 23.2, 23.45, 23.7, 24.0, 24.4, 24.8, 25.3, 26.25, 27.5, 28.5, 29.0, 29.3, 29.7, 30.55, 31.07, 31.5 and 32.43 s. I also read full-resolution crops of the back label (4.0, 4.5, 10.0 s), the pour (23.3-23.85 s) and the top of the outro (31.25 s). I computed frame-to-frame mean absolute difference and luma for every frame (160x90 gray), searched for loop seams, and recomputed per-segment motion_mean and jerk_median from timeline.json, using only the per-second bins that overlap each segment by at least 0.5 s.

Changes:
(1) Roast date. VERIFIED: the label is printed with 焙煎日 2026/09/22, but it is readable only at 9.2-10.4 s, not at 4-5 s. At 4.0 and 4.5 s the bottom line is out of frame or under the thumb. I moved the claim to segment 3 and to standout 10.0, and changed standout 4.5 to list what is actually readable there.
(2) Dropped the 'roasted to order' best-use. A printed roast date does not prove roasted to order. I added that the dated label will go stale.
(3) Loop for segment 1: loopable true changed to false. The probe's 0.0-3.2 s candidate ends on the back of the bag in the middle of the flip; the frames do not match (checked 0.0 against 3.2 s). The best seam inside the hold is 7.75/255. Only a ping-pong of 1.17-2.07 s works.
(4) Segment 1 tightened from 0-3 to 0.3-2.6 s: the flip starts at 2.64 s with blur and a luma lift, and there is a small jolt at 0.17-0.23 s.
(5) 9:16 crop set to null for segments 1, 2 and 3. The subjects are wider than the 0.316 window: the bag is about 0.40 wide; at 10 s the bag plus strip spans about 0.17-0.88. The first review gave 0.43, 0.53 and 0.5.
(6) Segment 2 changed to 3.2-8.4 s (the flip excluded). Recomputed motion 0.975, jerk 0.173.

inventory.summary: This is one continuous handheld shot from a high angle (about 45 degrees; it is not top-down) of four SNöBI frosted-white bags (Colombia, Mexico, Ethiopia, Peru) standing on an oak table in hard, warm window sun, with a large plant-like shadow across the table. A hand lifts the bags away (2.5-5.4s) and the empty table holds (5.6-8.3s). The camera then reframes and the lineup is rebuilt one bag at a time (Peru, Mexico, Ethiopia, Colombia), holding as a four-bag hero from 17.6s to the end. Its value is the hand-free beats (Peru alone, then 2, 3 and 4 bags), which can be chained into a 'the lineup builds' sequence once they are stabilised. That stabilisation must correct roll as well as drift.

inventory.verify_notes: I extracted and read frames at in+0.2, the midpoint and out-0.2 for every original segment, plus dense frames (0.1-0.3 s apart) over 2.4-5.5, 8.2-17.6 and the beat edges. I also read all six standout times, wrote a per-frame phase-correlation pass (fine.py: camera shift, residual motion after alignment, luma in 0.2 s bins) and ORB similarity fits between frame pairs (orb.py). All scripts and frames are in the scratchpad Z9M_6586 folder. Segment metrics are recomputed from timeline.json: windows [s, s+1) are confirmed by matching luma (s3 71.4 and s4 56.6 equal the fine-bin means), and a window is included when at least half of it lies inside the segment. CHANGES: (1) Summary: the shot is a high-angle three-quarter view (about 45 degrees) with the bags standing upright, not 'top-down'. The bags are lifted off one by one, not 'swept'. (2) Segment 1 tightened from 0-3 to 0.8-2.45. 0-0.8 is the camera settling (fine shift up to 2.9 px/frame at 480 wide), and the arm's shadow enters at the right edge at about 2.5 (residual 2.6->5.3, luma 108->92 by 2.8), not 3.0. Metrics are now s1 only: 0.483/0.161, so steady is true (was 0.683/0.226/false). (3) The segment 1 crop changed from 0.33 to null: the group spans x~0.14-0.90, far wider than the 0.316 window, and even the Ethiopia bag alone is about 0.315 wide. (4) The removal segment changed from 3-5.5 to 2.45-5.5. Motion 1.387 and jerk 0.191 (s2-s5) replace 1.623/0.155. The luma low is about 53 at 4.4-4.6 (fine bins), and I added the 'dark moment' flag. focus_ok changed from false to true, because the softness is motion blur (flagged), not focus. (5) The empty table is now 5.6-8.3 (clean from 5.6 after the bag's shadow exits; the reframe starts at 8.4). Its metrics (s6, s7: 0.252/0.151/steady) are confirmed. Framing changed from wide to medium: ORB scale is 0.998 between 7.0 and 10.5, so the camera distance is the same as the bag shots. The 9:16 centre moved from 0.55 to 0.62 to keep the light/shade edge and exclude the specks (x~0.34-0.46; the old window 0.39-0.71 included them). The speck location is corrected to y~0.24-0.40. (6) The build segment (8-17.7) is split into three. 8.3-9.7 is the reframe plus the Peru placement: camera 'handheld moving', steady false despite jerk under 0.25, because a reframe of up to 5.6 px/frame and a hand are visible. 9.7-11.2 is Peru alone, as a new segment with its own crop (0.37, valid only at about 10.2-11.0 or tracked, with no margin). 11.2-17.6 is Mexico, Ethiopia and Colombia, with motion 0.77 and jerk 0.222 from s11-s17. (7) Hand-free beat timecodes corrected from frames: Peru alone 9.7-11.2 (was 9.6-11.3; a fingertip is visible at 9.6 and the next bag at 11.25), Peru+Mexico 12.25-13.5 (was 12.6-13.6; the hand is gone by 12.2 and a shadow intrudes at 13.6), three bags 14.9-15.7 (was 14.8-15.8; a hand is at the top right at 14.8 and Colombia enters at 15.75). Framing drift between beats was understated: ORB shows rotation as well (10.5->20.5 about 6.5 degrees of roll and 100 px), not just '30-70 px'. I added the luma dips during placements. (8) The final hold starts at 17.6, not 17.7 (the hand is gone at 17.55; the residual drops to 1.23 at 17.6). Metrics 0.309/0.287/false are confirmed. The crop changed from 0.5 to null: the group spans x~0.12-0.93, and a 0.5-centred window (0.34-0.66) holds only Colombia, so a Colombia-only crop at about 0.51 is noted instead. Loopable stays true: 19.02 vs 22.22 has the same light (luma 129.6/129.8), and after an ORB similarity alignment (about 3 degrees of roll, 25 px) the mean absolute difference falls from 14.6 to 3.0. I added the roll flag. (9) Standouts: 1.5->1.2 (the frame-level shift is lower at 1.0-1.4 than at 1.4-1.8; Mexico's top label line is clipped at both times). 20.5->20.8 (shift 0.07 vs 0.57 px/frame), and I removed the 'best 9:16 crop (centre 0.5)' claim. 10.5 is called the 'smoothest' second (lowest jerk), since the lowest-motion second is s6. 7.0, 13.0 and 15.3 are confirmed by frames. (10) The shadow is described as 'plant-like' rather than 'foliage-like'. It is fixed relative to the table, so it is not the operator, but its source is UNKNOWN. CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: placement order Peru, Mexico, Ethiopia, Colombia and the final positions; label readability at 10.5, 13.0, 15.3 and 17.6+ (Ethiopia 'ETHIO', Peru 'P' only); hands only, with no faces anywhere (a dark green wrist band is visible); no hidden cut (one shot; all luma jumps trace to the arm's shadow); whole-clip measure values match clip.measure.json (shots 1, jerk 0.209, slowmo_share 1.0, L_mean 116.2).

inventory.summary: A 4.7 s handheld café shot, one continuous take. It opens for about 0.33 s on a La Marzocco drip tray with two small stainless cups. A fast whip pan left with a rising diagonal follows (0.33-1.77 s). It overshoots and jerks back right (1.77-1.97 s), then lands on a grind-by-weight grinder dosing magenta-looking grounds into a portafilter under blue LED light, with Torani syrup bottles on the left and an out-of-focus person in the lower-left foreground. The camera keeps drifting and bumping until about 4.1 s. Only the last 0.6 s is steady, and the clip cuts off mid-dose: the display reads 11.8 g and grounds are still falling. There are no SNöBI bags.

It opens on a dosed portafilter in the grinder fork under a blue and then red LED wash, with focus on the Torani syrup bottles beside it. The grade settles at 0.57, focus racks from the Torani label onto the mound (sharpest at 1.27), a hand comes in at about 1.7 and pulls the portafilter at about 2.4, and the camera follows it left and down through a dark, blurred move (luma 27.6 at 3.4). inventory.summary: One continuous 23.4 s handheld take at an espresso bar (a cafe, not the roaster). A young barista purges the steam wand (haze visible and a loud hiss on the audio from 0.6 to 2.4 s while the camera pans), wipes the wand with a cloth, brings a white pitcher to the wand at 6.2 s and steams milk until about 19.4 s, then turns off the steam, wipes the wand and brings the pitcher forward. The usable footage is the near-locked steaming close from 10.2 to 13.9 s (hands; the chin is at the 16:9 edge from 10.6 s) and the profile with eyes visible from 16.0 to 17.8 s. No SNöBI bag appears, and no steam is visible during the steaming itself.

inventory.verify_notes: Method: I extracted frames at in+0.2, the midpoint and out-0.2 for every original segment, plus all standouts, and read them. I also read 10 fps and 5 fps contact strips across the clip. A per-frame OpenCV probe (probe2.py in this folder) gave Laplacian sharpness, luma, phase-correlation shift and frame MAD; loop endpoints were compared by MAD over the full frame and the 9:16 window; the audio got a high-pass RMS check. Segment numbers use timeline.json samples whose 1 s window lies at least 50% inside the segment, the same convention as the first review. inventory.summary: One continuous handheld take at the bar, with no real cut. The 'second shot' that measure_film reports at 1.47 s is a false cut caused by motion blur. The barista picks up a cup of espresso and pours steamed milk (3.0–7.3 s), pauses while the crema marbles (7.3–8.9 s), then draws a swan latte (rosetta wing fronds, body, neck and heart head). The swan is held level in the palm (19.2–20.1 s), carried to a wooden bar and set down beside Torani syrup bottles, where the camera reframes and settles on the finished cup. The light is warm and the grade pushes the crema strongly yellow. There are no faces and no SNöBI bags or labels: this is cafe craft footage, with third-party Torani branding readable from about 23.2 s to the end.

inventory.summary: A single 39.5s take of a pour-over, shot outdoors in warm direct sun: a metal cone dripper on a fogged glass server, on a wooden table, against a stucco wall with leaf shadows and a snake plant. It runs in order: overhead dry grounds, water first touching the bed at about 2.1s, a continuous pour that builds the bloom foam until about 12.9s, a rise to a medium hold (15–17s), a tilt down to the server and a rise back up, a wide gooseneck pour (sharp from 22.5s, with the kettle body in the top-left from about 21.4s and the stream from about 24.4s), a push-in, and an elevated close-up of the foam settling after the pour stops at about 36.7s. There are no people and no SNöBI bags. The third-party embossed 'HARIO' wordmark on the black collar is legible in most of the clip: large at 0–0.7s and 12.5–21s, and low-contrast but readable at full 1080 resolution in the wide shot.

inventory.summary: An outdoor pour-over set piece in low, hard sun. A white gooseneck kettle, a steel cone dripper on a glass server (already about a third full of brewed coffee) and a SNöBI MEXICO Honey Chiapas DECAF pouch stand on a worn wood table, with leaf shadows moving on a warm stucco wall. It opens on a wide shot: kettle staging with handheld jolts (0 to 6 s), a calm hover (6 to 10.1 s), then a near-static wide where the pour starts at 10.1 s and runs to 12.5 s. A shaky, blurred handheld push-in follows (12.5 to 16.3 s). The clip ends on a bloom close-up that is in sharp focus only from 17.4 to 20.9 s. It is soft before that (16.3 to 17.4 s, with a pan jolt) and softens again after it (20.9 to 21.7 s).

inventory.verify_notes:
Evidence. Frames were extracted at in+0.2, the midpoint and out-0.2 for every original segment: 0.2/1.0/1.8, 2.2/4.0/5.8, 6.2/9.0/11.8, 12.2/13.5/14.8, 15.2/16.5/17.8, 18.2/19.0/19.8 and 20.2/21.06/21.92 s. I ran a per-frame diff, luma and sharpness scan (framediff.py, sharp2.py), a loop pair scan (loopscan.py), a background-patch exposure check (expo.py) and template tracking of the bag's logo/zip region against the 11.0 s frame (tmpl.py). All scripts are in the working folder.

Metric method. timeline.json is assumed to hold 1-second buckets [s, s+1). A segment uses every bucket it overlaps by at least 0.5 s; for the last segment the 0.12 s tail bucket s22 is included. All of the first reviewer's motion_mean and jerk_median values for its own bounds recompute correctly: 1.028/0.305, 0.645/0.275, 0.461/0.166, 1.632/0.191, 0.522/0.163, 0.967/0.196 and 0.457/0.186.

inventory.verify_notes:
Method: I extracted frames at in+0.2, midpoint and out-0.2 for every segment plus every standout moment, and built 0.5 s and 0.2 s contact sheets. I took native-resolution label crops at 0.2, 1.5, 12.0, 20.0, 22.5 and 26.0 s. I wrote sharp.py, peak.py and peak2.py (scratchpad/footage/Z9M_7208) to compute a per-frame focus peak (99th percentile of 64x64-tile Laplacian variance at 1920x1080), phase-correlation shift and luma. width.py measures pouch width, and seg2.py recomputes motion and jerk from timeline.json.

CHANGES:
(1) Segment 0–3 tightened to 0.0–2.8: the right hand reaches the label by 3.0 s (frames 2.5 / 2.7 / 3.0).
(2) The claim 'label + logo sharp' at 0–3 s is refuted. The label is crisp only at 0.0–0.5 s; at 1.5 s it is soft at native resolution, with focus on the top seal and thumb (focus peak 1842 vs 409–576). Standout moved from 1.5 to 0.2 s.
(3) Nail colour corrected from burgundy to dark red-brown. Logo colour corrected from grey to plum or dark purple (16.8 s frame and the 1.5 s crop).
(4) Segment 3–8 starts at 2.8 and focus_ok changed true → false: focus peak is 12 at 4.0 s, and 6.5–7.9 s is soft. 'Logo faint' corrected: the logo is clearly readable from 3.2 to about 6 s.
(5) Segment 8–11 changed to 8.0–11.9 s. Focus loss runs the whole span (peak 5–31), not just 9–10.4 s. Stats recomputed over s8–s11: motion 1.653, jerk 0.169. Sticker description added (handwriting, purple and peach sticker, '...COFFEE').
(6) Segment 11–18 split. 11.9–16.4 s is focus hunting (focus_ok false; stats s12–s15: 1.286 / 0.1725); the 12.0 s label is sharp only at 11.95–12.15 s (per-frame peak 973–4951, otherwise 23–90), so it is a still grab, not an insert. New segment 16.5–17.9 s: the front-on logo moment. The claim 'front at 16 s, then back to the seal at 17 s' is wrong: 16.0 s is soft, the bag is front-on and sharp from 16.5 to 17.9 s, and the hand returns to the seal at 18.0 s. steady set false because of the 17.1–17.4 s jolt.
(7) Segment 18–30 split into three. 18.0–21.0 s is the sharpest and steadiest stretch (jerk median 0.159). 21.0–28.2 s is soft at 21–25 s (22.5 s crop confirms), has the label partly covered at about 22–25 s (24.0 s frame), and ends in a left whip at 27.45–28.15 s that timeline.json misses. 28.2–29.63 s is sharp again. 'Label readable throughout' is refuted. 'Drifts right 0.5→0.65' is corrected: the pouch drifts right to about 0.62–0.71 at 26 s, then whips back to about 0.51.
(8) All crop_9x16_centre_x set to null. The pouch measures 0.39–0.43 of the frame width as a bright blob and up to 0.50 visually at 0–21 s, which exceeds the 0.316 window. The proposed 0.58 / 0.60 / 0.45 / 0.62 windows would cut the pouch. Label-only centres are given in flags.
(9) Standout 26.0 s replaced with 28.6 s (26.0 s focus peak is only about 250). Standout 16.8 s added.
(10) New defects: label table misregistration (VERIFIED visually at 0.2, 12.0 and 20.0 s); all-zero barcode (VERIFIED); focus hunting map; the uncaught whip; logo hidden from 18 s on; mid-dark green frame against the house rule of a light, daylight world; possible red mark on the hand (INFERRED); the company address is legible. 'Leaf Earth' corrected to the organic JAS mark with certifier 'Leafearth' (VERIFIED in the crops).
(11) best_uses rewritten: label inserts are now conditional on the label being fixed, and vertical-crop advice is changed.

AGREED / CHECKED UNCHANGED: single shot with no hidden cut (shots 1; luma changes are gradual, with no step); measure values (jerk 0.183, L_mean 93.4, slowmo_share 1); the original segment stats recompute exactly (0.389/0.159, 1.454/0.198, 1.804/0.182, 1.156/0.161, 0.524/0.1765); both probe loop candidates are not seamless (grid_loop.jpg); no faces anywhere; the bag never opens (seal intact at 29.43 s); jerk bumps at s6, s13, s22 and s23.

NOTE: the probe's steady_windows [10,13] and [15,22] ignore focus; 10–12.9 and 15–16.4 s are soft.

inventory.summary: This is one 22 s handheld take of two hands (no face) opening a 100 g SNöBI Peru whole-bean bag in front of dark green sacks and a burlap sack. The fingers work the top seam while the info label faces the camera. The bag then turns to show the SNöBI wordmark as the tear-to-open strip is pulled off, the zip is pried open, and the camera pushes in on the beans before pulling back out of focus. Three windows are usable: a steady label read (1.0–3.5 s), a native-speed brand insert (5.8–6.35 s), and a sharp, steady, loopable bean close-up (16.0–17.7 s). The rest is hand action with jerk or focus problems.

inventory.verify_notes:
Checked 40+ extracted frames (in+0.2, midpoint and out−0.2 for every original and revised segment, the loop endpoints, every standout moment, and full-resolution crops of the beans, wordmark and label). I also re-ran per-frame probes: tile Laplacian sharpness; LK-feature global translation, scale and acceleration (these include subject motion, so they are supporting evidence only); and a frame-difference loop search. Scripts and outputs are in this folder (verify_*.py, v_*.jpg, v_frames.json).

Changes:
(1) Re-segmented from 6 to 9 segments, with tightened in/out points. Original 0–5 became 0–1 lead-in (s0 jerk 0.277, motion-soft label), 1.0–3.7 label read (now steady: s1–s3 jerk 0.166/0.156/0.130) and 3.7–6.4 wordmark plus strip. Original 5–8 was split into 3.7–6.4 and an unusable 6.4–8.0 swing. 8–11 became 8.0–10.6. 11–15 became 10.6–16.0. 15–19.6 was split into 16.0–17.7 (sharp, steady by rule: jerk 0.198/0.151) and 17.7–19.7 (beans soft, s19 jerk 0.275). 19.6–21.92 became 19.7–21.92. Stats were recomputed from timeline.json, including each second that overlaps a segment by at least 0.5 s (verify_segstats.py). All the original segment stats were correct for their original boundaries.
(2) 'Back label' was wrong. The info label shares one face with the SNöBI wordmark (frames 5.2, 5.9 and 6.2 show both), so at 0–3.7 s the hand is covering the wordmark on the same face.
(3) 'Wordmark hidden 0–5 s, readable only 5.4–6.5 s' was wrong. The wordmark is readable from about 4.0 s (frames 4.1 and 4.8), and together with the label at 5.0–5.4 s and 5.8–6.35 s.
(4) Brand standout moved from 5.6 to 5.9 s. A full-resolution crop shows 5.6 s is motion-blurred, while 5.2, 5.9 and 6.2 s are sharp.
(5) The strip is the tear-to-open strip above the zip, not a 'reseal' strip.
(6) Bean reveal: beans are visible from about 10.7 s, not 11.3 s. Added the reframe jolt at 10.5–10.9 s and the soft patch at 11.7–12.6 s. The reveal standout moved from 11.4 to 11.1 s, and 13.2 s was added as the cleanest reveal frame.
(7) The camera in the bean hold is not 'near-locked'. The push-in runs from about 11 to 16.3 s (feature scale rises steadily, which the frames confirm), then there is a slight pull-back to 19.7 s and a fast pull-back after that. The camera label on the reveal segment changed to 'slow push', and the end segment from 'slow pull' to 'handheld moving'.
(8) The focus claim 'crisp' was too strong. Full-resolution crops show the beans sharp only at about 16.0–17.3 s (and about 13.0–13.5 s). At 15.1, 15.5, 18.0, 18.7 and 19.6 s the focus is on the bag rim. The 15–19.6 segment was set to focus_ok false for the 17.7–19.7 part. The standout at 17.5 moved to 17.0 s (steadiest moment, still sharp).
(9) Loop: the probe's 15.62→19.22 s endpoints do match (compared side by side), but the loop contains a ~12% push and pull and soft beans at both ends. I found a better loop at 16.05→17.65 s (difference 8.22 vs 10.71) with sharp beans throughout and verified its endpoints visually.
(10) End focus loss starts at about 20.2 s, not 20.5 s, based on tile sharpness and the 20.76 s frame.
(11) The 'green cast' defect was corrected. The measured colour is warm and neutral (a −0.7, b +12.4), and the green comes from the background objects. The clip is also mid-key throughout (luma 75–107 out of 255), not only in the dips.
(12) Crop centres: 3.7–6.4 changed from 0.5 to 0.54, because a 0.5 window clips the label's right edge at about 0.69. The zip segment changed from 0.6 to null, because hands plus bag span about 0.42 of the width. The reveal changed from 0.57 to 0.58. The bean hold changed from 0.57 to 0.55 (beans span 0.44–0.65). The swing and end segments are null.
(13) Organic JAS mark marked INFERRED, and roast level marked INFERRED.

Verified unchanged: no face anywhere in the clip (contact sheet plus all extracted frames); 1 shot with no hidden cut (the 9-point luma drop between s9 and s10 is the reframe onto the dark sacks); label text (Peru, 100 g, 2027/04/20, 2026/09/22, フローラル・みかん・ティー); and the measure values, which match clip.measure.json (shots 1, jerk 0.223, slowmo 1.0, L 97.6).

inventory.summary: One continuous overhead handheld take of an empty pale stoneware plate on a warm-brown wood table. The plate stays empty until 16.37s. From 16.37s to about 20.8s light-to-medium roast beans rain in from above the frame, bounce, and settle in two loose crescents with a sparse centre. The camera is nearly still from 17.0s to 20.4s. It then nudges sideways, rises off the plate from about 21.2s, and whips down to the floor from 22.0s, ending on table legs and window sun on a speckled grey floor. There are no people, no hands, and no SNöBI bag or label anywhere in the clip.

inventory.verify_notes:
Method: I extracted and viewed frames at each segment's in+0.2, mid and out-0.2 (0.2, 2.0, 3.8, 4.2, 10.2, 16.2, 16.6, 19.35, 22.1, 22.5, 23.97, 25.43), each standout (16.5, 18.5, 20.0, 21.9, 24.5), plus a per-frame tile of 16.2-16.7s, a 5 fps tile of 20.4-21.8s, and frames at 20.7, 21.0 and 21.6. I recomputed timeline.json stats per segment: the first review's numbers matched its own bins exactly (0.706/0.228, 0.246/0.229, 1.047/0.128, 4.761/0.101). I added a per-frame pass in fine.py (phase-correlation camera shift, plate-only and table-edge lightness), checked loop endpoints by frame difference and by eye, and ran a 2x minterpolate test on 18.3-18.7s. clip.measure.json values (shots 1, jerk 0.136, slowmo 1.0, L 114.4) and the 25.63s duration are VERIFIED.

CHANGES:
(1) Re-segmented from 4 segments to 6. The old 4-16.4 hold now runs 4-14.4, and 14.4-16.37 is split off as pre-pour shake (camera 10-13 px/frame, jolt about 45 px/frame at 15.5s, timeline jerk 0.356). The rain segment is tightened from 16.4-22.3 to 16.37-20.45: the camera is near-still only from 17.0s to 20.4s, nudges at 8-12 px/frame from 20.45s, and drifts up from 21.2s. A new 20.45-22.0 segment covers settled beans on a moving camera. The whip now starts at 22.0s, not 22.3s (16-23 px/frame at 22.0-22.6s).
(2) Recomputed stats for the new boundaries: 4-14.4 uses bins 4-13 (0.201/0.22); 14.4-16.37 uses bins 14-15 (0.47/0.30); 16.37-20.45 uses bins 16-19 (1.02/0.109); 20.45-22.0 uses bins 20-21 (1.102/0.211, steady false because 0.211 is over 0.20 and the camera nudges and drifts).
(3) First bean: enters at 16.37s and lands at about 16.43s, so the standout moves from 16.5 to 16.43. Beans settle by about 20.8s, not 21.8s.
(4) Standout 21.9 moved to 21.0: at 21.9 the camera is drifting about 8 px/frame towards the whip, while 21.0 is settled and sharp. Standout 20.0 rewritten: 'densest' is not supported, since subject motion peaks at 17-18.5s.
(5) Light dip corrected. The old claim was plate luma 155→128, about -17%, 'greyer and cooler', cause a vessel shadow or cloud. Measured plate-only L* is 60.8 at 10s, 57.6 at 16s and 54-56 at 18-21s: about -6% across the pour, and about 5% of the pre-pour drop already happened before any beans (camera angle). Table-edge luma stays flat at about 78 from 4s to 21s, which rules out a cloud. Plate b* rises from 3 to 5, so the plate does not turn cooler. Whole-frame luma falls 114→84 because beans cover the plate.
(6) The empty-plate hold changed from loopable true to false. The 7.81/10.81 probe pair shows the plate shifted about 5% of frame width and a changed glaze reflection; 7.0/10.4, 5.07/7.77 and 6.04/12.41 are no better (mean abs diff 6-12.5).
(7) 9:16 crop. The plate is 0.62-0.85 of frame width, against a 0.316 window, so the crop is null for every plate segment (was 0.45, 0.45 and 0.48). The rain segment is set to 0.47 because the falling streams (x about 0.40-0.58) fit the window; the claim that 'the plate fills the frame' in 9:16 was wrong.
(8) Optical-flow ghosting moved from NOT VERIFIED to VERIFIED: the interpolated frames smear the falling beans. Best use now plays at native speed.
(9) Framing changed from medium to close for the plate-filling segments.
(10) Descriptions: 'light-roast' became light-to-medium (by eye, INFERRED); 'walnut table' became warm-brown wood, mid-century legs (species INFERRED); 'concrete' became a speckled grey floor (INFERRED); 'ring around an empty centre' became crescents left and right around a sparse centre.
(11) Added findings: pale possible-quaker beans in the settled pile (VERIFIED in a 21.0s crop); a faint moving glaze reflection at 8-11s; the 16.5-16.8 phase spike is bean content, not a camera bump.
(12) 'Soft focus' at 0-1s reworded to motion softness: the camera moves 5-18 px/frame there.

Confirmed unchanged: no people, hands, faces, bags or labels anywhere; frame 15.5 is blurred; the green object at the left edge around 24s is not a readable bag; frame 24.5 is sharp; the whip section is unusable as motion. Scripts and frames are in the scratchpad: footage/Z9M_7236/fine.py, plate.py, fine.json, slowtest.mp4, slowtest_tile.jpg.

inventory.summary: High-angle close shot of medium-roast beans on a warm light-grey ceramic plate on a wood table, lit by soft warm daylight from frame RIGHT. For the first 10.3 s a loose two-lobed heart/tree arrangement of roughly 70-80 beans sits still while the handheld camera reframes (0-4 s), drifts (4-9 s), and bumps at 9.1-9.7 s. It settles by 9.8 s. The first bean drops in from out of frame at 10.38 s and hits the centre at 10.44 s. The pour scatters the design into a hollow ring (14-15 s) and builds a full pile; the last beans land at ~18.15 s and everything is still by ~19.5 s. From ~21.7 s the camera lifts and the pile drifts out of focus, and the take ends with a blurred whip at 23.6 s. No people, hands, vessel, bags or labels appear.

inventory.summary: One continuous handheld shot, looking down at an angle, of roasted beans on a pale grey ceramic plate on a warm wood table, framed close so the plate fills the frame. A loose, roughly heart-shaped scatter of beans sits still (0–3.8 s). Beans then fall in from above the top edge in two waves, with no hand or scoop ever in frame: the first bean at 3.83 s, a sparse trickle at 4.5–4.9, the main stream at 5.1–7.2, a short lull, then a second wave at 7.65–9.0. Everything has settled by 9.35 s, and the clip ends on a dense pile that is near-still until about 12.45 s, followed by a small camera reframe. There are no people, bags or labels; the light is warm daylight and the exposure does not change.

inventory.verify_notes:
Method: I extracted the frames in, at the midpoint and out of every original and corrected segment and every standout moment (v_*.jpg, w_*.png) and read them, along with 100% crops (cmp_focus_early.jpg, cmp_pourstart.jpg, cmp_settle.jpg, cmp_top.jpg). I also wrote scripts in the clip folder: cam_lk.py (per-frame LK feature track for camera dx/dy, zoom and moving-point share), pairreg.py (SIFT registration between frame pairs), rimreg.py (ECC on the plate rim and table only, so spreading beans cannot fake a zoom), sharp.py (Laplacian sharpness), diffmap.py (aligned difference maps) and cam_probe.py (probe-style motion and jerk over arbitrary windows). Metrics come from timeline.json bins that overlap a segment by at least 0.5 s, the same convention as the first review. The first review's arithmetic was correct for its own segments.

inventory.summary: One continuous handheld shot of green (unroasted) coffee coming out of a white machine. inventory.summary: One continuous 16 s handheld shot, square-on to the drum roaster's front plate. The bearing flange is at the top, two stainless hinges sit above a small sight window full of tumbling green beans, and the chrome U-bar of the discharge chute is in the foreground. A blue cable runs down each edge; the right one ends in a white-sleeved probe fitting. The beans look olive/khaki with no browning, so this is probably early in the roast (INFERRED). The camera holds (0-3.2 s), tilts down slowly (3.2-5.1 s), pushes in to about 1.15x (6.0-7.9 s; closest around 7.8-8.1 s) and pulls back to about 0.95x by 10.7 s. It then holds, with the stillest stretch at 10.7-11.9 s and one slow vertical drift and return at 12.3-15.7 s. The frame is low-key and machine-heavy, so it is only usable as the film's one dark beat.

A hand (with a link-bracelet smartwatch and a ring) feeds a white Tokyo Coffee decaf bag into the jaws. The bag lies upside-down, so the arc wordmark and the lime DECAF MEXICO sticker read inverted. The camera tracks the bag along the jaws, arcs round to the outfeed and then loses it. The only premium-grade beat is 15.0-17.6 s, where the bag slides out of the outfeed under a near-still camera (not locked). Several sub-second bumps and focus misses that the 1-second timeline hides break up the rest.

standout_moments.why: Crisp panel detail: 190 on the temp display and glowing green and red switches. It is not person-free, because a hand holding the bag (with a watch) fills the right edge. Use a punch-in on the display and switches. The frames before 0.45 s are a pan-in.

The bag is gripped by the band with the hand steadying it. The wordmark, sticker and snowflake are all sharp, but the label is upside-down. The mouth entering the jaws happened at about 5.3 s, inside a tilt bump, and the hand lets go at 7.0-7.4 s.
3/4 travelling parallax view as the bag rides the jaws on the teal belt, a strong diagonal with no hands. The third-party nameplate is readable at upper left and the label is inverted.

Hero frame: the sealed bag slides out past the black knurled pulley onto the teal belt under a near-still (not locked) camera with peak bag sharpness. Build the sealing beat on 15.0-17.6 s at 50% slow-mo. The label reads upside-down.

The hand grips the finished bag at the belt end, sharp on the hand, watch and ring. It is a possible 'done' cut, but it must end by 20.45 s (the arm whip starts at about 20.5 s) and it is only about 0.5 s long.

best_uses: Roast-day film, 'sealed one bag at a time' beat: 15.0-17.6 s at 50% optical-flow slow-mo gives about 5.2 s on screen. It is machine-driven motion with no hands, which fits the slow-subject rule; check the warp on the inverted label text.
Travelling process shot: 10.5-12.4 s, tracking along the jaws with parallax and no hands (about 3.8 s at 50%). Keep it short or punch in past the readable third-party nameplate.
Detail insert: 0.5-2.3 s with a 16:9 punch-in on the temp display and switches (about x 0.25-0.47) so the hand and bag at the right edge drop out.
Website process still: a frame at about 16.5-17.3 s (bag on teal belt, peak sharpness). The upside-down label means it reads as a process image, not a product label shot.

9:16 Reel or Story: no crop keeps the whole bag (it is 0.45-0.56 of frame width against a 0.316 window). The only option is a label-only crop at about x 0.64 on 15.0-17.6 s, which loses the pulley and is untested.
defects: 0.0-0.45 s: pan-in or settle at the head (about 17 px/frame of horizontal flow at 0.1 s, soft frames). Start at 0.5 s or later.

5.1-5.5 s: camera tilt bump (about 75 px vertical in 0.4 s, fine-grained jerk about 4x the hero level). Luma rises 102 to 117 with the reframe. It lands exactly on the bag mouth entering the jaws, so the 'into the sealer' moment is not clean.
9.0-10.5 s: the camera swings to follow, the bag goes soft (bag sharpness 13-22), and a quick vertical jolt at 10.2-10.45 s (about 12-13 px/frame) is not visible in the 1-second timeline.

12.4-15.0 s: arc round to the outfeed with focus on the machine and the bag soft (sharpness 11-25 against 95 in the hero), plus a vertical settle at 14.1-14.4 s. Focus lands on the bag only at about 14.9-15.0 s, so the earlier review's 14.0-14.9 s was not clean.
17.6-19.8 s: focus slides off the bag from 17.6 s, a hard bump at 18.1-18.4 s (timeline jerk 0.352), then everything is soft.
20.5-21.62 s: an arm whips across the lens (flow about 27 px/frame, luma 121 to 141 in about 0.2 s), ending on a blurred wooden table with other bags. Cut by 20.45 s, not 20.8 s.
The label is upside-down for the whole clip: the arc wordmark and the DECAF MEXICO sticker read inverted, and rotating the frame is not an option. Any label-forward use reads awkwardly.
The SNoBI name is never legible; the bag reads as Tokyo Coffee plus DECAF MEXICO with a snowflake. That this is a SNoBI bag is INFERRED, not confirmed.
The third-party sealer maker's nameplate (Japanese company name and address) is readable at about 8.5-11.9 s and partly visible 7.2-8.5 s.
Hand actions at 0.5-7.4 s and 19.8-20.45 s carry optical-flow warp risk at 50% slow-mo.
A dark-cased smartwatch on a metal link bracelet is visible at 0-5.3 s and 19.8-20.45 s, and a ring at about 5.3 s and 20.0 s (one person is INFERRED). No logo is visible.
Background clutter: wire shelving with loose bags, papers and a blue cable at the left from about 12.5 s to the end.
Exposure is mostly gradual (luma about 101 at 2-4 s to about 127 at 14-17 s), but it steps 15 points in 0.4 s at 5.1-5.5 s (reframe) and about 20 points in 0.2 s at 20.5-20.7 s (arm).
inventory.verify_notes:
Method: I extracted frames at in+0.2, the midpoint and out-0.2 of every original segment (0.2, 3.0, 5.8, 6.2, 10.0, 13.8, 14.2, 16.0, 17.8, 18.2, 19.81, 21.42), at every standout (0.5, 6.8, 11.0, 16.5, 20.0) and at extra probe points (0.05, 0.9, 1.3, 1.8, 2.3, 5.0, 5.35, 7.2, 7.6, 9.8, 10.3, 10.7, 11.8, 12.3, 13.2, 14.0, 14.9, 17.6, 18.3, 19.2, 20.4, 20.6), plus full-resolution label crops at 6.5, 11.2 and 16.8 s. I recomputed per-frame Farneback flow, flow-difference jerk, luma and Laplacian sharpness (whole frame and the bag region) into scratchpad fine.json, and ran a phase-correlation shift check. Segment motion_mean and jerk_median come from timeline.json samples whose 1-second window overlaps the segment by at least 0.5 s: A uses s=0-4, B s=5-8, C s=10-11, E s=15-17, F s=18-19. The original four segments' numbers recomputed exactly (1.084/0.188, 0.951/0.11, 0.459/0.152, 2.392/0.167), so its arithmetic was VERIFIED, but the 1-second timeline hides sub-second bumps.

Changes:
(1) Split the original 0-6 s segment into 0.5-5.0 and 5.5-9.0. I dropped the 0-0.45 s pan-in (VERIFIED: flow about 17 px/frame and soft frames) and the 5.1-5.5 s tilt bump (VERIFIED: about 75 px vertical, luma 102 to 117), which the first review missed. That bump covers the actual mouth-into-jaws moment.
(2) Original 6-14 s: the hand releases at 7.0-7.4 s, not 6-7 (VERIFIED: fingers on the bag at 6.8 and 7.2, gone at 7.6). 9.0-10.5 s is soft with a 10.2-10.45 s vertical jolt, and 12.4-15.0 s is the arc with the bag out of focus, so I kept only 10.5-12.4 s as a separate tracking segment.
(3) Original 14-18 s hero: tightened to 15.0-17.6. Focus lands on the bag only at 14.9-15.0 s (bag sharpness 12 to 83), and focus starts sliding at 17.6 s (100 to 57 by 17.8 s). Camera changed from 'locked' to 'handheld drift': framing drifts about 4-6% (VERIFIED by comparing 14.9, 16.5 and 17.6 s; flow 1.4-2.7 px/frame). 'Drive pulley' is better described as a black knurled pulley or knob.
(4) Original 18-21.62 s: retimed to 17.6-20.45 s. The whip starts at about 20.5 s, not 21.0 (VERIFIED: flow 16-27 px/frame and luma 121 to 140 at 20.59-20.79 s), so the cut point moved from 20.8 to 20.45 s. The 20.45-21.62 s whip is listed as a defect only.
(5) Every crop_9x16_centre_x is now null. The bag is 0.45-0.56 of frame width against a 0.316 window. The original 0.58 window on the hero (0.42-0.74) excludes the pulley at x about 0.30-0.35, so its claim that the crop 'keeps the bag, the label and the pulley' is false. The original 0.68 and 0.74 windows also cut the subject.
(6) Labels: the bag is upside-down throughout (VERIFIED in the full-resolution crops). The original wording 'label facing camera' and 'readable' was corrected to 'sharp but inverted'.
(7) Standout 0.5 s: 'no person in frame' is false, because a hand with the bag and watch is at the right edge. Standout 6.8 s: the hand is still on the bag and the mouth entered at about 5.3 s, so I moved it to 6.5 s and reworded. Standout 20 s: moved to 20.2 s with cut-by 20.45 s.
(8) People: 'black smartwatch' at 1-6 s and 'steel-band' at 20 s look like the same dark-cased link-bracelet watch, and a ring is visible at both 5.35 s and 20.0 s, so one person is INFERRED.
(9) best_uses: the hero is now 15.0-17.6 s (about 5.2 s at 50%, not 6 s), the panel insert starts at 0.5 s not 0.3 s, and the travelling no-hands option 10.5-12.4 s was added.
(10) Added defects: head pan, 5.1-5.5 s bump, 9.0-10.5 s soft and jolt, 12.4-15.0 s soft arc, the inverted label, and a corrected exposure note (two short luma steps, not purely gradual).

Unchanged and VERIFIED: the 190 temp display, the panel text, the nameplate, the never-legible SNoBI name, the background clutter, measure values (shots 1, jerk 0.166, slowmo_share 1, L_mean 125.2 from clip.measure.json), and loopable=false everywhere (first and last frames differ in every segment; the probe's best loop diff is 39.6). Phase-correlation responses were low (0.08-0.28) because of parallax and a moving subject, so the drift sizes are approximate (INFERRED from the frame comparisons).

inventory.summary: This is one continuous handheld band-sealer take with no real cut. It opens on the heat controller reading 190, dips down and back up, then a hand feeds a kraft gusset bag into the sealing jaws. The camera tracks the bag as the machine carries it past the vented heater body and the drive pulleys and onto the teal conveyor, where hands lift it. The label reads 'ode by TOKYO COFFEE / EXTINCTION' (VERIFIED in full-res crops at 6.0, 10.2 and 17.9 s), so this is a Tokyo Coffee ode bag, not a SNöBI-branded one. The clean cores are 8.2–10.8, 12.5–15.0 and 17.4–18.2 s; from 18.6 s to the end the picture is soft and fast.

inventory.summary: This is one continuous handheld take of a batch drop at the drum roaster. It opens on the discharge chute and its bean window, seen from a 3/4 angle and then head-on. It whip-tilts up to the drum faceplate, where an operator's hand works a port, then tilts back down as the hand swings the door open and the batch pours into the cooling tray. It ends on about 19 s of the cooling tray, where the stirring arm sweeps the dark bean bed while the camera holds three framings, with two reframing moves in between. No SNöBI bags, no labels and no faces appear. The only people visible are one operator's hands.

inventory.verify_notes:
Method: I extracted about 75 frames (each segment's in+0.2, midpoint and out-0.2, every standout, every loop endpoint, and 0.5 s steps through the tray) and looked at them. I recomputed every stat from timeline.json. I added a per-frame global-motion pass with phase correlation at 1080p px/frame (fine.json) and a skin-pixel detector for hand timings. The scripts are in the scratchpad folder: segstats2.py, fine.py, binf.py, skin.py, loopscan2.py.

The first review's arithmetic is correct as written (VERIFIED), but its boundaries and several claims are wrong. Changes:
(1) Seg 0-6.11 split into 0-3.4 (shaky: 5-14 px/frame, a start jolt up to 39 px/frame, steady=false, motion 1.28, jerk 0.248) and 3.5-5.5 (steady, jerk 0.195, loopable 4.1-5.3 with diff 9.39, endpoints compared). 'people: none' was wrong for the tail: fingers are at the right edge from 5.5 to 6.1.

The fingers are not 'about 12-17 s'; the exact intervals are 11.7-12.45, 13.8-14.25, 14.8-15.95, 16.2-16.8 and 17.2-17.5 (VERIFIED with the skin detector and frames 11.8, 12, 12.2, 14, 15.5). The 10.9-12.9 loop claimed 'no hand', but fingers cross inside it, so it is clean only in a 9:16 crop. No hand-free 16:9 loop exists (best diff 21.3). I added that the chute is wider than a 9:16 window: the crop keeps the window and the chute's centre.
(4) Added the whip-tilt segment 17.5-19.4. The settle ends at about 19.4, not 17.95 (18.0-18.9 still runs at 12-25 px/frame).
(5) Drum face retimed to 19.4-28.4: jerk median 0.329 (seconds 20-27), not 0.312. The camera barely translates (1-2.7 px/frame), so the hand drives the jerk (INFERRED). Crop moved from 0.70 to 0.76 to hold the port and hand. 'Wedding ring' is now 'ring' and 'sample port' is marked INFERRED.

The first review's 'possibly a different operator' is unsupported: both hands wear the same type of square smartwatch on a link band and a ring, so probably the same operator (INFERRED).
