concepts.surface: /origins/[slug] (the origin page is the product page): a module directly under the buy card, with the add-to-cart button staying above it. Plus a still chip on the shared ProductCard (home and /coffee), shown on hover or focus and always visible on touch. No video on cards.
concepts.what_viewer_sees: 0.0-2.5 s at real speed: a Peru 100 g bag held toward the lens, fingertips picking at the tear notch, info label facing us. At 2.5 s it holds on the 2.8 s frame and a thin plum ring (SVG over the video, not burned in) draws around the printed line 焙煎日 2026/09/22. Beside it in page type: 「見本：2026年9月22日（火）焙煎の袋」. Under that, a live line computed by code, for example 「火曜と金曜に焙煎。次の焙煎 10月9日（金）→ 発送 10月13日（火）」. 2.5-2.9 s: 10-frame dissolve. 2.9-6.1 s: the same bag open, whole beans with pale centre cuts filling the mouth, at 50%, looping every 3.2 s under 「豆のまま。挽くのは淹れる直前に。」. On cards, a one-line chip rises from the bottom edge: a crisp still crop of the 焙煎日 line plus 「焙煎日は袋に」.

clips.treatment: Real speed: fingers and label text would warp under interpolation. Steady already (jerk 0.156), light stabilise optional. Freeze on the 2.8 s frame (sharpest window is 2.5-3.2 s). Desktop 4:5 crop centred at 0.55. Mobile 9:16 at 0.55, keyframed to follow the label as it drifts from x 0.48 to 0.58. If the label check fails, punch in at 2x or more on the 焙煎日 line using the camera original.
50% optical flow gives 3.2 s. Seamless loop with a 0.4 s crossfade (endpoint diff 8.22; beans sharp throughout). Same crop as above. Check frame by frame for warps on the nail edges and the bag rim.
Still for the card chip: tight crop of the 焙煎日 line only, pulled from the camera original, not the 1080 proxy.

concepts.why_it_works: The buy block is where doubt lives. In under 6 s, one take of one real bag proves two live claims: the roast date is printed on the bag, and the beans are whole. The computed line then turns the claim into a date the buyer can plan around. The specimen agrees with the schedule: 2026/09/22 is a Tuesday (computed). On the grid, the date is the line's sharpest edge against supermarket organic, and a still chip says it without adding video noise to the cards. The 3D scene already turns the bag to the stamp; this is the real stamp. Side note for the video session: this label read is the only footage that crops to 9:16 for the spot's 'label' beat (centre 0.55). That is a pointer only, not a storyboard change.
concepts.rule_check: Two shots. The opening hold is 2.5 s (meets the 2 s minimum). One 10-frame dissolve. The bean shot runs at 50% and is smooth (jerk 0.198 and 0.151). Rule bent on purpose: the label beat plays at real speed, because interpolation smears text and fingers. Real footage, hands only (consent covered). Muted H.264, about 3 MB at 1080. Poster is the 2.8 s frame. Reduced motion shows the poster plus a bean still at 17.0 s. The copy never says 'roasted to order' or 'we show our work'. Buy route stays above the module.
concepts.risks: 1) LABEL. On Z9M_7208 (same Peru bag, same lot 2026/09/22) the label table is VERIFIED misregistered, with values sitting one row below their headers, and the barcode reads 0000000000000. The 7209 label is legible at 1080 and INFERRED to carry the same print. If confirmed, either show only the 焙煎日 line (a separate bottom line) or fix the label and reshoot. Bags may be shipping with this label, which is a food-labelling problem beyond the site. 2) The printed date ages, so it must always carry the 見本 caption and never read as the buyer's bag. 3) Peru footage appears on all four origin pages. Either add 「どの袋も同じ表示」 or, on Ethiopia's page, use Z9M_6572 at 9.3-10.4 instead, which is unsteady (jerk 0.342) and has a luma swing. 4) The ship date must be computed by code from one registry entry. Roast weekdays alone currently have about 10 copies (site-plan, VERIFIED), plus order cutoff (UNKNOWN), a JP holiday list and business days. For example, Mon 10/12 is スポーツの日 (INFERRED), so a Friday roast ships Tuesday. Until the cutoff exists, show only the line already in cart.tsx: 「火・金焙煎。焙煎日翌営業日に発送。」 (VERIFIED). 5) The near right hand is soft in the lower right of the bean shot.
concepts.depends_on: Full-res check of the 7209 label table and barcode, with a label fix and one-bag reshoot if it fails. Camera originals for the punch-in and chip. Registry entries for roast weekdays, order cutoff (owner), JP holidays and ship rule, read by one function. Owner OK on the 見本 caption.

concepts.name: The plate fills to free shipping (add-to-cart moment)
concepts.surface: Cart drawer (components/commerce/cart.tsx), next to the ShippingProgress line. Desktop: a 1:1 tile about 280 px. Mobile: no more than 30% of the drawer height, collapsing once it settles.
concepts.what_viewer_sees: The buyer taps カートに入れる and the drawer slides in. 0-0.8 s: a still of a loose heart of about 65 roasted beans on a pale grey plate in warm daylight. 0.83 s: one bean streaks in and rolls. 1.5-1.9 s: a sparse trickle. 2.1-4.2 s: the main stream rains, splits the heart and scatters beans to the rim. 4.35 s: it stops on a half-built pile with nothing falling, and the line under it reads, live, 「あと¥440で送料無料」. When a later add pushes the subtotal past ¥3,000, the second wave pours (2.0 s), the pile settles, the line becomes 「送料無料」, and the tile breathes in a 2.9 s near-locked loop. A single add that crosses on its own (Peru 200 g, ¥4,720) plays straight through in 6.35 s. Removing items never reverses the pour; a 10-frame dissolve goes to the state the new subtotal implies.

clips.treatment: Real speed. 50% interpolation ghosts the falling beans (VERIFIED with an ffmpeg minterpolate test). Stabilise 3.0-3.83 locked to the 3.0 s frame (static plate; jerk 0.403 there) so poster and playback match. 1:1 crop centred at 0.47: the heart (x 0.22-0.70) and the stream (x 0.40-0.56) both fit. Stop on the 7.35 lull frame, where nothing is falling, and use it as the 'half' poster.
Real speed, second wave. Plays only when the subtotal crosses the threshold. Same crop.
Real speed, settled-pile loop. Camera within about 6 px; 0.5 s crossfade at the seam. Cut before 12.45 s, where the camera reframes. Poster at 10.0 s.

concepts.why_it_works: The free-shipping threshold is the one number that changes basket size, and today it is a text line. Binding the plate to the subtotal turns the threshold into an object: the pile is visibly half built. Prices in content/products.ts (VERIFIED) put every 100 g bag under ¥3,000 (Colombia ¥1,410, Ethiopia ¥1,605, Mexico ¥1,610, Peru ¥2,560), so a first add of a 100 g bag stops on the half pile. The clip's own lull at 7.2-7.6 s is that stopping point, with no fake cut. Beans pouring is a slow natural subject, and the buyer's action triggers it, not scroll.
concepts.rule_check: One take with two stop points inside a real lull. No hidden cut. Muted. Rule bent: plays at real speed instead of 50%, because interpolation ghosts the beans (VERIFIED). Code picks the clip state from subtotal and threshold, so footage never computes anything. Reduced motion shows three stills (heart, half, full). Not scroll-driven, not parallax. Warm daylight plate.
concepts.risks: Could read as a gimmick, so A/B test it against a static still. Lazy-load after the first add; three clips at 720 px 1:1 come to about 1.5 MB (INFERRED). The beans carry no bag, so never caption an origin; a decaf buyer sees light-to-medium beans. Falling beans render as pale streaks (slow shutter) and read as rain. Luma falls from 133 to 81 as the plate fills, so the full state looks heavier. ¥3,000 is a literal in shipping-progress.tsx (VERIFIED) and has about 15 copies in the site (site-plan); it must come from one registry entry that matches the Shopify shipping profile. Two Colombia 100 g bags (¥2,820) correctly stay on the half pile, though some buyers may expect a fill per add.
concepts.depends_on: Registry entry free_shipping_threshold, read by cart.tsx and shipping-progress. Stabilise pass on 3.0-3.83. A subtotal-change hook in the cart.

concepts.name: Read the bag: four claims, four printed lines
concepts.surface: /coffee, section 2 (below the four cards), headed 「袋に書いてあること」. /faq's freshness and organic answers link to it.
concepts.what_viewer_sees: 0-1.45 s at real speed, on the wooden desk in hard striped sun: hands pull the Ethiopia Guji bag's tear strip across the frame and the white bag swings into the sunlight. 1.45 s: it freezes on the 10.0 s frame, with the whole back label readable and the strip extended. Then, 0.4 s apart, four hairline plum leaders draw from printed lines to page type: 「豆のまま」 for whole bean; 「有機コーヒー豆」 plus the organic JAS mark for organic; 「焙煎日 2026/09/22（火）」 for the roast date on every bag; 「製造者 株式会社ローグトレード 東京都東久留米市」 for roasted in Tokyo. Tapping a callout zooms into that line (still crop from the camera original).

clips.treatment: Real speed: the thin strip and label text warp under optical flow. Start after the tab-tear jolt at 8.41-8.48. Light stabilise only, because the hand and strip are moving. Freeze on 10.0 (the reviewed frame where the whole label, including 焙煎日, is readable). 16:9; on mobile, crop 4:5 centred about 0.5 on the label.
Fallback still for zoom crops of the bottom half (製造者 address, organic JAS/Leafearth mark, flavour line), if they are not crisp at 10.0. Camera original.
Fallback still for the title line 'Snöbi Ethiopia Guji 100 豆のまま' and 有機コーヒー豆. Camera original.

concepts.why_it_works: Every live claim is checked against something printed on a real bag in real daylight. The label is the evidence, and the page only points at it. One frame carries four proofs. The 'Tokyo' claim gets a printed address instead of an adjective. The tear-strip moment is the most tactile 'first open' in the footage, and the desk sun is the brand's 'one real object in daylight'.
concepts.rule_check: One real-speed shot, then a still. Rule bent on purpose: no 50% slow-down, because the strip and text would smear. Callouts are HTML/SVG, never burned in, so they stay crisp and translatable. Hands only. Poster is the 10.0 frame. Reduced motion shows the still with callouts already drawn. Headline avoids 'we show our work'.
concepts.risks: STOP condition: the label-table misregistration and all-zero barcode are VERIFIED on Z9M_7208 (Peru) and UNKNOWN on this Ethiopia label. A magnifier over a non-compliant label is worse than no label. If either shows up, fix the template, reprint, and reshoot one bag on the same desk in the same light; the setup is easy to repeat. Other risks: 10.0-10.3 s is the brightest stretch (luma peak 167), so check the label text for clipped highlights. A green watch band and khaki trouser edge sit at the right edge. The label's flavour line (ティー・ドライフルーツ・ベリー) must match content/products.ts before any callout cites it (single source). That the 製造者 address is also the roasting site is INFERRED and needs owner confirmation. The date ages, so always caption it 見本.
concepts.depends_on: Full-res label check on 6572 frames 4.0, 4.5 and 10.0 (table order and barcode). Camera originals for the zoom crops. Owner confirms 東久留米市 is where roasting happens. Roast weekdays from the registry (the weekday shown is computed, not typed).

concepts.name: The lineup builds (Coffee page header)
concepts.surface: /coffee header (the new Coffee page), sitting directly above the four ProductCards. Desktop and mobile both use a 16:9 band. Kept off Home so it never sits beside the 3D 'four bags line up' scene.
concepts.what_viewer_sees: 0-2.2 s: the Peru bag alone on an oak table in hard window sun, a plant-shaped shadow across the wood, slowed and near-still. Dissolve. 2.2-4.0 s: Mexico (DECAF) now stands beside it. Dissolve. 4.0-5.6 s: Ethiopia joins behind. Dissolve. 5.6-8.6 s: Colombia front-centre, all four together. The shot keeps breathing on a 6.4 s loop while the buyer reads the cards below. Type sits only in the shaded wood at upper left.

clips.treatment: 50% optical flow gives 2.2 s. Safe: static bag, no hands (fingertip gone by 9.65, next bag enters at 11.25). Stabilise and align to the 20.8 s frame with roll correction.
50% gives 1.8 s. Hand-free beat; both labels legible. Align with roll correction (about 1.7° and 85 px from the Peru beat). 10-frame dissolve in.
50% gives 1.6 s. Hand-free; Ethiopia reads only 'ETHI'. Align. 10-frame dissolve in.

50% gives 6.4 s. Stabilise to a locked frame with about 3° of roll correction (aligned seam diff 3.0, against 14.6 raw), then loop with a short crossfade. The first 3.0 s is the closing shot. Overall crop-in is about 10-20% to absorb up to 6.5° of roll and 100 px of drift between beats.

concepts.why_it_works: The buyer's job on /coffee is to pick one of four. The film sets them down one at a time, then ends on the exact lineup the grid lists below it. Peru, the flagship Geisha, lands first. Real bags in real sun, with no hands, read as a shop shelf, not an ad. Nothing in the frame is printed with a date, so it never ages.
concepts.rule_check: 4 shots. Opening hold 2.2 s (minimum 2). Median shot 2.0 s (target 1.5-2.0). Close 3.0 s (minimum 2.5). 10-frame dissolves as the only transition. Every shot at 50%, all on static subjects, smooth after stabilising (raw jerk 0.089 for the Peru beat, 0.287 for the final hold before stabilising). Autoplays once when in view, then loops. Not scroll-pinned. Muted. Under 5 MB at 1080. Poster is the 20.8 s frame; reduced motion shows the poster.
concepts.risks: A 10-20% crop-in on the 1080 proxy goes soft, so the camera originals are needed (higher resolution INFERRED). In the final hold Peru's label is half hidden and Ethiopia's is clipped to 'ETHIO'; the cards below name them. No 9:16 or 4:5 crop holds the group (it is 0.8 of frame width), so mobile gets a short 16:9 band. Roll correction can expose warped edges. Specks on the table only appear in the empty-table plate, which is not used. It is a still life with dissolves; if the owner wants more motion, this is the wrong slot.
concepts.depends_on: Camera originals. Stabilisation with roll correction. The /coffee page (site-plan Phase 2).

concepts.name: Same sun: the real bag after the 3D bag
concepts.surface: /origins/[slug], the section directly after the drag-to-rotate 3D bag: a 4:5 clip beside two lines of text, above the facts and buy card.
concepts.what_viewer_sees: The visitor has just spun the 3D bag. Next comes the real one, in film: Ethiopia, held up in hard striped desk sun and barely breathing, on a seamless 3.6 s cycle. Peru, alone on the oak table in window sun, settling over 2.6 s and then resting on its sharpest frame. Colombia and Mexico, each front and centre of the four on the same oak table, its label fully readable, neighbours soft at the crop edges, on a 6.4 s breathing loop. Caption: 「同じ袋を、窓の光で。」

clips.treatment: Ethiopia. Stabilise (raw jerk 0.287). 50% optical flow gives 1.8 s, played forward then reversed (3.6 s cycle). This is the only clean loop: frame change under 2.3/255 here, so the reversal is invisible. 4:5 crop centred 0.45 (bag about 0.40 wide; about 0.025 margin each side). Poster at 1.5.

Peru. 50% gives 2.6 s, played once, resting on the 10.5 s poster. Not loopable: drifts 0.07 of width and luma climbs 124 to 136. 4:5 crop centred 0.37, keyframed to follow the drift, or stabilise first.
Colombia. Stabilise with roll correction, 50% gives 6.4 s, loop with crossfade. 4:5 crop centred 0.51; Colombia (huila) fully readable.
Mexico. Same stabilised loop, 4:5 crop centred on the right-hand Mexico bag (about 0.75, INFERRED from 'Mexico right'; measure before cutting). MEXICO and DECAF fully readable.

concepts.why_it_works: The 3D bag is a promise; the film is the receipt. Same pouch, real light, before the buyer reaches the price. Three of the four come from one table, one sun and one take, so the four pages read as one shelf. Ethiopia's desk is the same warm, hard daylight. Desire comes from texture: the frosted film, the label, the sun. No copy is needed.
concepts.rule_check: One muted loop per page with a poster; reduced motion shows the poster. 50% only on near-static subjects with no hand motion (Ethiopia's hands hold still; consent covered). Ping-pong counts as seamless under the web-loop rule. Under 3 MB each. No text over bags.
concepts.risks: Colombia and Mexico are recentred crops of one shared shot, so a visitor who opens both pages sees the same frame twice. Accept that, or reshoot each bag alone on the 6572 desk in the same sun (about 10 minutes; owner call). The 3D model's label art must match the real pouch, or the cut exposes the difference. Ethiopia: the green watch band at lower right may stay inside the 0.45 window. 4:5 crops from the proxy are 864 px wide and soft on retina, so use the originals.
concepts.depends_on: Camera originals. Measuring the Mexico x-centre in the final hold. Checking the 3D model against the real bag.

concepts.name: Decaf in the low sun (Mexico page brew pair)
concepts.surface: /origins/mexico, a 16:9 section under 'how to brew', after the real-bag section. This is the only origin with its own brew footage that shows its bag in frame.
concepts.what_viewer_sees: 0-2.5 s: a wide shot of an outdoor wooden table in low, hard sun, leaf shadows moving on warm stucco. A white gooseneck kettle pours a thin stream into a steel cone on a glass server, and the SNöBI MEXICO honey chiapas DECAF pouch stands beside it, label readable. Dissolve. 2.5-5.1 s: close on the stream falling into a pale bubbled foam pool ringed by dark grounds, sharp, slowed. Dissolve back to the wide; it repeats. Copy stays on brewing (ratio, temperature), not on claims.

clips.treatment: 50% optical flow gives 2.5 s. The camera is near-locked (0.02-0.13 px/frame). 16:9 only, because 4:5 cannot hold both dripper and pouch. A 1.05x punch-in anchored bottom-right removes the fingertips at the top-left edge. Check the thin stream for warps.

Stabilise (wander 0.3-1.5 px/frame), then 50% gives 2.6 s. This is the sharp window (foam Laplacian 122-287). 16:9, or 4:5 centred 0.47. Mask or retouch the HARIO wordmark ('ARIO') on the dripper collar. 10-frame dissolves in and out, looping back to the wide.

concepts.why_it_works: In specialty, decaf's barrier is that it reads as the compromise cup. Showing the decaf pouch beside a careful pour-over, in the long low light of late in the day, sells it as the coffee you can still drink at 5 pm, without saying so. Attribution is honest because the bag is in the frame.
concepts.rule_check: 2 shots. Opening 2.5 s (minimum 2), close 2.6 s (minimum 2.5). Dissolves as the only transition, looping by dissolve. 50% on a slow natural subject (stream and foam). Wide jerk 0.206, just over 0.20, but that comes from near-zero motion; the close is 0.129 after stabilising. Muted, under 4 MB. Poster on the wide at 11.4.
concepts.risks: Third-party HARIO wordmark is in the close-up, so mask it or accept it small. Continuity: the server is already about a third full before the pour; in 2.5 s it barely reads. The stream is thin at wide size. 'Late in the day' is INFERRED from the sun angle, so the copy must not assert a time. The true first bloom (Z9M_7052 2.0-7.9, CO2 bubbles from 3.2 s) is the stronger freshness image, but use it only if the owner confirms it brewed this decaf: same set, INFERRED, unproven.
concepts.depends_on: Stabilise pass. Owner decision on HARIO masking. Owner confirmation before adding the 7052 bloom.

concepts.name: Trade: the range at the counter, then the chain behind it
concepts.surface: /trade. The hero is a 16:9 band (1:1 on mobile). Below it, a static three-tile row headed 「仕入れの流れ」 (stacks on mobile); not a pinned or horizontal-scroll strip. Each tile carries one fact line read from the registry.
concepts.what_viewer_sees: Hero, 0-5.8 s: four SNöBI bags on a wood table in low side sun (Ethiopia guji sharp, Mexico DECAF, Colombia 'OLOMBIA huila'). In front of them, a glass server pours an amber stream into a glass mug and bubbles gather. It comes to rest on the half-full mug. Tiles, as muted loops: 生豆, green coffee raining onto a growing mound. 焙煎, beans tumbling and glowing behind the roaster window. 封緘, a sealed bag sliding out of the band sealer onto the teal belt, played once then held. Fact lines: 火・金焙煎 / 焙煎日翌営業日発送 / 100g・200g, plus wholesale size, MOQ and lead time once the owner supplies them.

clips.treatment: 50% optical flow gives 5.84 s. Hands-free and steady (jerk 0.153). Plays once and rests on the 21.5 s frame. Desktop 16:9; mobile 1:1 centred 0.67 (mug body, stream and full Ethiopia label; handle cut). Type goes only on the lower-left wood. Check for warps on the stream and bubbles.

生豆 tile. Real speed (shutter-streaked beans; test 50% only if warps pass). Loop with a 0.45 s crossfade (luma diff 1.2). 1:1 crop centred 0.55; check that the saturated blue bin corner at top-left falls outside.
焙煎 tile. 50% gives 2.4 s, seamless loop (diff 9.39), hand-free. 1:1 crop centred 0.45, which drops the kitchen timer and card at the right edge.

封緘 tile. 50% gives 5.2 s. Machine-driven with no hands; jerk 0.086. Plays once on view and rests on the 16.5 s poster. 1:1 crop centred about 0.55 to hold bag, tail and pulley (bag plus tail about 0.51 wide; measure). Check for warps on the inverted label text.

concepts.why_it_works: Café owners buy reliability, not romance. The hero puts the whole range at the counter in one frame, so it reads as 'stock all four'. The tiles show the chain they are buying into, green coffee to roast to sealed bag, on real machines with no stock and no farm-faking. The fact beside each tile is what they plan orders around.
concepts.rule_check: The hero is one shot at 50% on a smooth, hands-free subject, with a poster. Tiles follow the web-loop rule: muted, seamless or crossfaded, small, with a poster, and reduced motion shows stills. Static grid, not a pinned horizontal strip. No dark footage: the window tile is mid-key (luma about 73), and the drum close-up (7596) and cooling tray stay off this page. No faces.
concepts.risks: The 7669 bag's SNöBI identity is INFERRED (Tokyo Coffee arc wordmark, DECAF MEXICO sticker and snowflake; the SNöBI name is never legible), and its label is upside-down. Verify on the camera original. Never use Z9M_7695, which is VERIFIED as an 'ode by TOKYO COFFEE' bag. The 7289 green coffee is not verified as SNöBI's organic lot, so caption it 生豆, never 有機生豆. Which coffee is in the hero server is UNKNOWN; claim nothing about it. Espresso and latte clips (6788, 6790) are excluded: nothing proves SNöBI beans are in the cup, and La Marzocco and Torani marks dominate. Add them only if the owner confirms. Wholesale terms are UNKNOWN.
concepts.depends_on: Owner supplies wholesale sizes, MOQ and lead time into the registry (roast days and ship rule read from the same entries as the cart). Verify the 7669 bag identity. Measure the 1:1 crops.

concepts.name: Brand film 'One table, three falls' (33.8 s, type C)
concepts.surface: Story page header (click-to-play, sound on) and YouTube, 1920x1080 master. Could later replace the stills in the Home hero film; that is the owner's call.
concepts.what_viewer_sees: 0.0-2.6 Empty oak table in hard late-morning sun, a plant shadow across it, nothing moving (fades in from the footage's warm tone). 2.6-4.6 The Peru bag fades into the same sunlit spot through an aligned dissolve, with no hand; PERU is readable. 4.6-6.4 Green beans fall as one broad curtain onto a mound. 6.4-8.2 (dark passage begins) Green beans tumble behind the roaster's small sight window, punched in so the window fills the centre. 8.2-10.0 The drop: a dense wall of roasted beans spills over the stainless chute, camera locked. 10.0-12.2 Cooling tray: the black stirring arm sweeps slowly through the bed (dark passage ends). 12.2-14.6 Back to light: a sealed bag slides out of the band sealer onto the teal belt. Type '火曜と金曜に焙煎。焙煎日は袋に。' shows 12.8-14.3 on the lower-left belt, never on the bag. 14.6-16.4 The oak table again: Peru and Mexico, no hands. 16.4-18.2 The Ethiopia bag held up in striped sun, other SNöBI bags soft behind. 18.2-20.2 Top-down into the opened bag: glossy beans. 20.2-22.2 A heart of beans on a pale plate; the first bean streaks in at about 20.96 (source 10.38) and the heart starts to break. 22.2-24.2 Overhead: water meets dry grounds, the wet patch spreads, CO2 bubbles erupt at about 23.6-24.0. 24.2-25.4 The table: three bags. 25.4-27.8 Wide pour-over on the sunlit desk beside the MEXICO decaf pouch, leaf shadows on the wall. 27.8-30.2 A golden stream into a glass mug, the Ethiopia guji bag sharp behind. 30.2-33.8 All four bags on the oak table, held. From 31.0 the wordmark, 'オーガニックのまま、スペシャルティ。' and snobi.jp settle into the shaded wood at upper left. The last frame is the poster.

clips.treatment: 50% smooth_shot chain → 2.6 s (static plate, so no interpolation risk). Stabilise to locked and warp-align to shot 2's framing (about 65-70 px offset, same scale, ORB). Clone the white specks at x 0.34-0.46, y 0.24-0.40. 12-frame fade in from warm tone.

50% → 2.0 s. Stabilise and align so table and shadow stay still through the dissolve from shot 1: the bag appears and no hand is seen. Handles stay inside 9.7-11.2, before the next bag enters at 11.25.
50% → 1.8 s. Inside 3.6-6.9, where the blue bin corner is absent. Check the falling streaks frame by frame. Fallback: 100% 5.6-7.4 with a 3-frame blend.

100% with a 3-frame blend → 1.8 s, because the beans are baked-in motion streaks and the inventory says real time is safer. Stabilise to locked. 1.5x punch-in on the sight window from the 3840x2160 original (a 2560 px window, so no upscale).
50% → 1.8 s. Hands are clear from 32.2 and the camera is already locked. Clone out the white kitchen timer on the tray rim (x 0.83-0.97, static). Fallback: 100% 32.3-34.1.
50% → 2.2 s. Stabilise the 3-4 px/frame nudge at 54.0. Exposure +0.35 stop (source L about 34).
50% → 2.4 s. Light stabilise (4-6% drift). No crop. The label is upside-down, so type stays on the lower-left belt.
50% → 1.8 s, inside the hand-free window 12.25-13.5. Stabilise with roll correction and align to shot 2 (about 1.7° and 85 px) so the table doesn't jump. About 10-20% crop-in from the 4K original.
50% → 1.8 s. Stabilise (source jerk 0.287; bag nearly still here). 1.15x punch-in anchored left, from 4K, to drop the green watch band and the khaki trouser edge at the right.
50% → 2.0 s (the steady stretch, jerk 0.169). About 1.2x punch-in anchored upper-left, from 4K, to push the smartwatch face at lower right out of frame. Check frame 20.5.

concepts.why_it_works: This is a film the footage can tell truthfully: one Tokyo morning with no farm and no stock (all 26 clips were shot 11:03-12:00 JST on 2026-10-01 and graded with one LUT; VERIFIED, grade/README.md). Two devices carry it without words. First, the same oak table comes back four times and gains a bag each time (Peru, then +Mexico, then +Ethiopia, then all four), so the lineup builds across the whole film. Second, between those returns, everything that moves is falling: green beans, the roasted drop, beans onto a plate, water onto grounds, coffee into a mug. These subjects are slow by nature, which is what the house slow-motion rule asks for. The roast is the one dark passage, placed in the middle, so the film opens and closes in daylight on the same table. Only SNöBI's own bags appear; the café and Torani footage is left out.
concepts.rule_check: 16 shots in 33.8 s = 4.7 per 10 s (target 4-6). Open hold 2.6 s (target ≥2). Median 2.0 s: sorted lengths run 1.2 to 3.6 and the 8th and 9th are both 2.0, the top of the 1.5-2.0 band. Close 3.6 s (target ≥2.5). One device: 15 dissolves of 10 frames, plus a fade in and out through the footage's warm tone. 15 of 16 shots are slowed to 50% with smooth_shot.sh. Shot 4 (7596) is the exception at 100% plus blend, because its beans are baked-in streaks. Shots 3, 5 and 11 fall back to 100% if they ghost (ghosting is VERIFIED on 7236 and 7251 with minterpolate). Source jerk is at or below 0.17 for 11 shots. 6586 (0.222/0.287), 6572 (0.287) and 7703 drop (0.294, caused by the falling beans; the camera moves under 1.2 px/frame) are stabilised to locked first. Shortest shot is 1.2 s, so nothing approaches the rejected 0.5 s median. No illustration, stock, farm footage or parallax. Type sits only on empty areas, and only in real brand fonts or the wordmark SVG. One bend: the 'one dark moment' is read as one contiguous 5.8 s roast passage (drum, drop, tray at L 34-57), not a single shot.
concepts.risks: (1) Bag identity in the sealer shot (7669): the SNöBI name is never legible; the bag reads as Tokyo Coffee plus DECAF MEXICO plus a snowflake, so it being a SNöBI bag is INFERRED. If it isn't, cut shot 7: the film becomes 31.4 s with 15 shots. (2) Jerk on shot 5: v02's drop shot from the same clip measured 0.22 after the 50% chain (VERIFIED, renders/v3/v02.measure.json), so shot 5 will probably exceed 0.20 again. Fix: run it at 100%, or trim it to 1.2 s. (3) Interpolation ghosting on the falling-bean shots 3, 5 and 11 is VERIFIED for ffmpeg minterpolate; whether RIFE or Topaz does better is UNKNOWN. (4) The four returns to the table need roll and drift alignment of up to about 6.5° and 100 px. A 10-20% crop-in is an estimate (INFERRED), but it is affordable from 3840x2160 (VERIFIED). (5) A 1.2x punch-in may not fully remove the smartwatch in shot 10 (UNKNOWN). (6) smooth_shot.sh is proven on 1080 proxies only; how it performs on 4K masters, in time and quality, is UNKNOWN. Fallback: cut on the proxies, then conform crops from 4K with the same parameters. (7) The three-shot dark passage needs the owner to accept that reading of the rule. (8) No brew or pour shot is tied to a named coffee on screen, so there is no claim risk.
concepts.depends_on: An owner decision on the 7669 bag. A 4K ProRes conform (masters are not rendered yet, per grade/README.md). Brand fonts reachable by the HyperFrames renderer (Adobe kit xkh1hrz is a Dynamic embed; whether the renderer can load it is UNKNOWN), otherwise the wordmark SVG only. A licensed music track (bar ≈ 2.0 s, about 120 BPM, so dissolves land on bar lines). A frame-by-frame interpolation check on shots 3, 5, 11 and 12.

concepts.why_it_works: The footage was shot in the same session as the photos the storyboard uses: the grade README pairs six clips with photo framings (single bag, lineup, pour-over ×2, bag opening ×2; VERIFIED). Which clips those are is INFERRED to be 6586, 7052/7074 and 7209/7199. Swapping each still for its moving twin keeps the approved composition and look and adds real life: sun drift on the bag, CO2 bubbles, hands holding beans. Beat 3 stays a still on purpose. No footage holds the Peru front label art large and sharp, and the only footage label close-ups (the info label in 7199, 7208 and 7209) show a misregistered table and an all-zero barcode (VERIFIED in 7208; INFERRED to be the same label in 7199 and 7209).

Camera jerk after stabilisation is INFERRED to be near 0, with the remaining motion coming from the hands. Light world: L 101-136, with the arm-shadow dips being natural. The file is about 12.7 s at about 3.5 Mbps ≈ 5.6 MB (INFERRED, inside the 4-6 MB budget), H.264 with a poster. No faces, no third-party marks, type on shaded wood only.

(3) The 10-20% crop-in for roll correction is an estimate. (4) Mobile shows a small 16:9 image. (5) If the owner wants the Home 3D bag scene to stay the only lineup moment, this belongs on /coffee only.

scores.name: Home hero: from an empty cup to a full one (real footage replaces the Ken Burns stills)
rule_violations: Shot 2 (drop) runs at 100% between three 50% shots, so the speed changes mid-film. The bend is documented but the shift will be felt.
It retires the owner-approved Home 3D scroll scene, which is a structural change to the approved Mockup D and needs the owner's decision.
clip_errors: Shot 3 (7237 0.6-1.3) is a styled bean-on-plate shot. That contradicts the concept's own reason for excluding the 7236/7244/7251/7266/7273 plate set as 'styled, any brand'.
Shot 2's 3:2 window at 1.02x anchored left ends at about x 0.827. The timer starts at 0.83, so the margin is zero and the timer edge may show.
7111 18.8-21.5 at 50% is 5.4 s against a 5.0 s slot (4.8-9.8). That only works with dissolve overlap; check it in the edit.
The opening lineup hides Peru, the flagship (only 'PE' shows), on the most important frame of the site.
scores.note: The narrative is right: bags and an empty cup, then the real drop, then the cup filled. The clips are honest and the crops check out. It is weakened by the generic plate insert and the 50%/100%/50% speed jolt, and it depends on killing the approved 3D scene. Cut the 7237 shot, run it as three shots, and take it to the owner as a choice between this and the 3D scene. Do not ship it by default.

scores.name: Coffee page: the four arrive
rule_violations: Median shot is about 1.5 s, at the bottom edge of the 1.5-2.0 band.
clip_errors: The final hold has only 'P' for Peru and 'ETHIO' for Ethiopia, so the end frame does not name all four.

The empty-table plate is about half in deep shade with concrete at top left and sits about 70 px off the build framing. Alignment plus a 10-20% crop-in on the 1080 proxy goes soft, so it needs the camera originals.
scores.note: This is the strongest Coffee-page header: the 3D 'four bags line up' idea done with real bags in hard window sun, and the empty-table opening gives it room. All in/out points sit inside verified hand-free windows. It is the same idea as 'The lineup builds' and 'One-take Four arrive', and this is the best version of the three. It is not a slideshow only if the roll alignment is perfect. Swimming shadows in the dissolves would make it read cheap.

scores.name: Origin pages: 'after it reaches Tokyo' coda (the 3D bag keeps the signature and gets the live roast date)
clip_errors: Ethiopia 6572 19.7-22.15: the black smartwatch face is prominent at lower right from 13-22 s and will probably survive a 4:5 crop at 0.53.
Colombia has no clip of its own; it is a recentred crop of the shared 6586 lineup hold, which also feeds the Coffee loop.
The Mexico wide has a thin stream that is hard to read at that size, and fingertips need a punch-in.
scores.note: The placement is honest ('東京に届いてから', captioned Tokyo) and the live roast date on the 3D bag is a good single-source move. But four small end-of-page clips, two of them borrowed, are low impact. Merge it with 'Same sun' (the receipt right after the 3D bag), and use the Decaf brew pair for Mexico.

scores.name: About/Story: the drop (the site's one dark band)
rule_violations: Every shot runs at 100%, not 50% (a documented bend because falling beans ghost when interpolated).
clip_errors: The door shot (29.7-31.9) keeps the hand, smartwatch and ring on the handle until about 31.9. It is acceptable, but it is the least premium frame in the band.
scores.note: No other brand can show this, all timecodes match the inventory, it cuts only on the camera's own moves, and it ends on the one verified seamless mechanical loop. It is the right home for the site's single dark moment. 'One-take The drop' is the leaner alternative; choose one.

scores.name: FAQ: the bloom inside the roast-date answer
clip_errors: The origin of the coffee in 7052 is UNKNOWN, so a caption that ties it to SNöBI freshness overreaches.
scores.note: It is clean and cheap, but a bloom is the most generic coffee image there is, and hiding it in an accordion caps its impact. It is fine as a small proof but adds nothing distinctive. Do it only if the FAQ already has the media slot.

scores.name: Trade: one espresso stream beside the inquiry
rule_violations: It fails the 'would fit any coffee brand' test: a stock-like espresso stream with no SNöBI identity.
clip_errors: Neither the venue nor the beans are proven to be SNöBI, so the panel implies a product it cannot show.
scores.note: It is beautiful but generic, and the owner explicitly rejects that. 'Trade: the range at the counter' does the same job with SNöBI bags in frame.

scores.name: Cart: the drum window next to the roast-day line
rule_violations: Dark machinery motion inside the checkout path, the highest-friction point, against the light-world rule.
clip_errors: At about 160 CSS px the olive-green early-roast beans read as raw or murky, and the window is mostly motion streaks.
scores.note: Drop the video and keep the real win: replace the hard-coded cart literal with a registry-derived nextRoastDay(). Motion at checkout is a distraction tax for almost no proof.

scores.name: Journal: the first Roastery post, green to sealed
rule_violations: Dim figures (7290 at luma about 95, the tray at about 35) against the light world. Acceptable inside an editorial, as the concept says.
clip_errors: 7669: the SNöBI identity of the bag is INFERRED and the label is upside down. Figure 5 is conditional.
7289/7290 green beans read grey-beige and a blue bin intrudes, so both need grading.
scores.note: This is the right place for honest footage that is too long or too dim for the commerce pages, and its exclusion list is excellent and accurate. It is low impact by nature but costs little once the Journal exists. Five figures in one post is a lot; four is enough.

scores.name: 焙煎日は袋に: the bag, opened (roast date and whole bean from one take)
rule_violations: The label beat runs at real speed, not 50% (a documented bend).
It magnifies a probably non-compliant label: misregistration is VERIFIED on the same lot in 7208.
clip_errors: 7209 label: the 7208 defects (rows shifted, barcode 0000000000000) are INFERRED to apply here too. That is a STOP until checked at full resolution.
The frame is mid-key with dark green sacks (luma 75-107), not the daylight world.
A single Peru take would appear on all four origin pages.
scores.note: Strong buyer-proof thinking: the computed ship line and the 見本 caption are exactly right, and the weekday arithmetic checks (9/22 is a Tuesday, 10/9 a Friday). But it puts a magnifier on a label that is probably defective, in a dim scene. Fix the label and reshoot one bag in daylight, or merge it into 'Read the bag'.

scores.name: The plate fills to free shipping (add-to-cart moment)
rule_violations: A gamified UI gimmick, which is the cliché/'mid' territory the owner rejects.
Motion in the cart drawer.
clip_errors: 7251 0.4-3.8 jerk is 0.462 (every second over the ceiling). Even 3.0-3.83 needs locking.
The plate fills from luma 133 to 81, so the 'success' state looks heavier and darker.
scores.note: The timecodes are precise and the use of the lull is clever, but a progress bar made of a styled bean plate fits any coffee brand and reads as a trick. Make the registry threshold fix without the video.

scores.name: Read the bag: four claims, four printed lines
rule_violations: 8.55-10.0 is hand action at jerk 0.342 (s8), over the 0.30 ceiling, played at real speed.
clip_errors: Luma swings 112 to 167 inside the shot (peak 10.3). The 10.0 freeze sits on the bright swing, so check for clipped label text.
The label table and barcode compliance is UNKNOWN on this Ethiopia label (the 7208 Peru defect is VERIFIED). That is a STOP condition.
The claim that the 製造者 address is the roasting site is INFERRED.
scores.note: The idea is good: the label is the evidence and the page only points at it, in desk daylight. But the moving part is a 1.45 s shaky tear, and the whole piece rests on an unverified label. Make it a still, or reshoot a clean bag on the same desk. Pick this or '焙煎日は袋に', not both.

scores.name: The lineup builds (Coffee page header)
clip_errors: The final hold has 'P' for Peru and 'ETHIO' for Ethiopia only.
Peru at 10.0-11.1 includes drift (0.07 of width) and a luma climb from 124 to 136; the calmest part is 10.4-11.1.
scores.note: A near-duplicate of 'Coffee page: the four arrive' and slightly weaker, because it has no empty-table opening. Fold it into that concept.

scores.name: Same sun: the real bag after the 3D bag
rule_violations: The real-bag clip sits right after the 3D bag. Ensure only one moving element per viewport (needs the media governor).
clip_errors: The Mexico 4:5 centre of about 0.75 is INFERRED and must be measured.
The Colombia and Mexico pages show the same frame recentred.
Ethiopia's 0.45 4:5 window leaves only about 0.025 margin per side, and the green watch band may intrude.
scores.note: 'Promise, then receipt' is a stronger placement than the end-of-page coda, and the Ethiopia ping-pong is the one verified clean loop of that bag. But three of four pages come from one shared take. Worth it only with a 10-minute single-bag reshoot per origin in the same sun. Merge with the origin coda.

scores.name: Decaf in the low sun (Mexico page brew pair)
rule_violations: Only 2 shots, under the 4-6 per 10 s envelope (acceptable for a section loop, not a film).
clip_errors: The HARIO wordmark is on the collar through the whole close-up (17.6-18.9), so masking is mandatory.
The server already holds coffee before the pour (a continuity issue).
'Late in the day' is INFERRED from the sun angle.
scores.note: The only brew footage with an origin's own bag in frame. The low hard sun and leaf shadows are cinematic, and the decaf framing is honest. Timecodes sit in the verified near-locked and sharp windows. Mask HARIO and it is the Mexico page's footage.

scores.name: Trade: the range at the counter, then the chain behind it
rule_violations: The hero plus three simultaneous muted loops on one page breaks the one-signature-move discipline.
clip_errors: 7669 bag identity is INFERRED and the label is upside down.
The 7289 1:1 crop at 0.55 needs a check that the blue bin corner stays outside the window.
Which coffee is in the hero server is UNKNOWN.
scores.note: Better than the espresso concept because SNöBI bags carry the hero. The tile row of loops is busy, and the wholesale terms that make it useful don't exist yet. Ship the hero, with stills for the tiles (or one moving tile).

scores.name: Brand film 'One table, three falls' (33.8 s, type C)
rule_violations: The 'one dark moment' is stretched to a 5.8 s, three-shot roast passage (a documented bend; needs the owner's OK).
Shot 4 runs at 100% while the rest run at 50%.
clip_errors: Shot 12 (7052 2.3-3.3) starts after first contact (2.07-2.14), so 'water meets dry grounds' is not on screen; start at 2.0.
Shot 5 (7703 drop) measured jerk 0.22 after the 50% chain in v02, so it will likely fail again.
Shot 11 (7244 plate heart) is styled plate footage that other concepts reject as generic.
The 7669 bag identity is INFERRED.
scores.note: The most ambitious and the most ours: a real 'one Tokyo morning', the returning-table device that builds the lineup, and 'everything falls' as a motif. Shot lengths and the sum (33.8) check out. The middle order (open bag, then plate, then bloom) wanders; tighten it to about 25 s and drop or replace the plate shot. It needs 4K conforms and frame-by-frame interpolation QA.

scores.name: 10 s spot: same six beats, real footage in four of them
rule_violations: Beat 2 changes the approved device ('three bags slide in' becomes a framed plate). That edges into the storyboard owned by the video session, so it must stay a proposal.
clip_errors: The beat-1 9:16 crop at 0.37 has zero margin (bag 0.30 in a 0.316 window), and the 28 px rise needs overscan that trims the bag.
Beat 5 (7209) sits against dark green sacks (luma 88-90) in a paper world.
scores.note: Correct, respectful use of footage as moving twins of the approved stills. Every crop and timecode matches the inventory, and the v02 error notes (7074@15 sits in the push-in, 7703@31 still has the hand) are valuable. Hand it to the video session as an option, not a change.

scores.name: Reel 1/4 'Green, then brown' (three falls, 10.8 s)
rule_violations: All shots run at 100% rather than 50% (a documented bend for ghosting).
clip_errors: The 7266 stream renders as a translucent grey streak, so the plate fall is weaker than the drop.
The 7596 9:16 crop loses the hinge symmetry; the window is a small streaky subject.
scores.note: One clear idea that only a roaster can post: green into the bin, out of the drum, onto the plate. All crops are verified 9:16 survivors, and the match dissolves on centred falling columns are smart. The best of the reels.

scores.name: Reel 2/4 'One revolution' (cooling tray loop, 7.4 s)
rule_violations: Entirely dark as a standalone piece (L about 34), against the light-world rule.
clip_errors: The arm period of about 3.7 s is INFERRED from loop lags, so check the seam at full speed.
scores.note: A genuinely seamless, hypnotic loop with type taken from live facts, at almost no cost. But an all-dark reel off-brands the light world. Better as the Story-page loop (already in the About concept) than as a standalone post.

scores.name: Reel 3/4 'First water' (bloom one-take, 9.5 s)
rule_violations: A generic bloom that fits any coffee brand.
clip_errors: The red channel clips on 9-11% of the frame, which may fall inside the crop.
The coffee is UNKNOWN, so nothing ties it to SNöBI.
scores.note: Clean and well timed, but every specialty account posts this exact shot. It adds nothing that says SNöBI. Keep the bloom inside the brand film only.

scores.name: Reel 4/4 'Open a Peru' (8.7 s)
rule_violations: Shot 2 (12.8-13.8) is a push-in at jerk 0.256-0.280, with sharp beans for only about 0.5 s.
clip_errors: The probably misregistered info label sits near frame from 3.7-6.4; the out-point at 4.9 must hold.
Dark green sacks (L 75-107) and a soft near hand filling 30-40% of the crop.
'Light roast.' over beans that read light-to-medium in the grade.
scores.note: The allowed strings and the flagship are well used, but the scene is the dimmest bag footage and dodges a label defect. Cut shot 2 (6.7 s version) or wait for a daylight reshoot of a fixed bag.

scores.name: One-take 'Four arrive' (type A, 12.7 s)
rule_violations: Fast, motion-blurred hand placements at real speed (placement bins at jerk 0.22-0.35), which is not premium.
clip_errors: Ethiopia is never fully readable ('ETHI' and 'ETHIO'), and Peru ends as 'P'.
Stabilising a 12.7 s take with up to 6.5° of roll while hands enter and leave makes the crop-in an estimate.
scores.note: The timecodes are accurate and there are no cuts, but blurred arms dropping bags in real time read as behind-the-scenes, not cinematic. 'Coffee page: the four arrive' edits the hands out and is clearly better.

scores.name: One-take 'The drop' (type A, 8.7 s)
rule_violations: Real speed, not 50% (documented).
clip_errors: 29.6-32.1 is handheld with the hand, watch and ring on the handle; it needs stabilising into the locked section.
scores.note: Honest and decisive, and all the event times are verified (door 29.86, hand gone 32.2, empty 37.7, tilt 38.4). It is the same material as the About/Story drop band. Choose that version, which ends on the tray loop, and keep this as the fallback.

scores.name: Home hero: from an empty cup to a full one (real footage replaces the Ken Burns stills)
rule_violations: The drop shot runs at 100% instead of ~50%. This is a documented bend and is acceptable.
Retiring the owner-approved Home 3D scroll scene (Mockup D) is out of scope for this concept. It needs an explicit owner decision, so it is not a rule pass.
clip_errors: 7111 4.4-5.5 VERIFIED inside the steady 4-9 s window. The 3:2 window anchored right (x 0.156-1.0) clears the server sliver (0-0.12); the arithmetic holds.
7703 32.4-34.2: the 3:2 crop at 1.02x anchored left ends at about x 0.827. The timer starts at 0.83, so the margin is about 0.003; measure it on the original.
7237 0.6-1.3 is fine, but it is the only plate shot and it is static texture. The 0.29 jerk bin means stabilising is mandatory, not optional.
7111 18.8-21.5: the hands are gone at 18.8 (VERIFIED). The stream crosses the Colombia and centre-back label text at 50%, so interpolation will warp it. This is a real risk, not hypothetical.
scores.note: Strongest site concept, and every timecode checks against the inventory. Duration math also checks: 2.2+1.8+1.4+5.4 minus 3 dissolves is about 9.8 s. The bytes (~3.5 MB) are plausible. Effort is understated: stabilising, the speck patch, the warp check, grade-matching a dark beat between two daylight tables, and rewiring Home are M+. Decouple it from retiring the 3D scene and ship the film either way.

scores.name: Coffee page: the four arrive
clip_errors: All five 6586 windows fall inside the inventory's hand-free beats (6.6-7.6 plate, 10.2-11.0, 12.4-13.3, 14.95-15.65, 19.02-22.22). VERIFIED.

The empty-table plate is about 65-70 px off the build framing and rolls about 2.6 deg inside itself. Its luma (101-109) is well below the Peru beat (124-136), so the first dissolve will show a brightness step as well as the alignment problem.
The specks at x 0.34-0.46, y 0.24-0.40 sit in the middle of the plate and need a clean-plate patch on every frame, not a one-off.
The final hold shows Peru as 'P' and Ethiopia as 'ETHIO', and the three-bag beat shows only 'ETHI'. Two of the four origins never read fully in the closing frame.
scores.note: This is the same idea as concept 12 and concept 22; build only one of them. This version adds the empty-table opening, which reads nicely but costs the most alignment work (6.5 deg of roll and 100 px across the beats, plus the plate offset). Effort L is honest. Camera originals at 3840x2160 are VERIFIED (grade README), so the crop-in is affordable.

scores.name: Origin pages: 'after it reaches Tokyo' coda (the 3D bag keeps the signature and gets the live roast date)
clip_errors: 6586 9.7-11.2: the fingertip leaves at 9.65 and the next bag enters at 11.25, so the in and out points are tight but valid. The 4:5 window (0.45 wide) at 0.37 holds a 0.30-wide bag. VERIFIED.
7074 10.1-12.5: fingertips stay at the top-left until about 12.2. The 1.08x punch-in that removes them is INFERRED and not measured.
6572 19.7-22.15: the black smartwatch face is prominent at lower right from 13 to 22 s. A 4:5 crop at 0.53 (0.305-0.755) will very likely keep it. The steady window itself is VERIFIED.
Colombia reuses the 6586 final hold. A 4:5 crop at 0.51 keeps parts of Peru and Mexico at the edges.
scores.note: Placing Tokyo footage after the farm content is honest and well reasoned. The live roast-date stamp on the 3D bag is the best idea here. But two of the four pages reuse the /coffee frames, and the Ethiopia watch problem is unsolved. Merge this with concept 13; one real-bag slot per origin page is enough.

scores.name: About/Story: the drop (the site's one dark band)
rule_violations: Every shot runs at 100%, with no 50% shot at all. Shot 1 (the angled window, which loops 4.1-5.3 at 50%) and shot 5 (the tray arm) could be slowed but aren't, so the envelope bend is broader than it needs to be.
clip_errors: 7703 3.5-5.5: the fingers enter at the right edge at 5.5, which is the out point exactly, so there is no margin. The 4:5 crop at 0.45 excludes the right edge, so this is acceptable.
7703 29.7-31.9: the door opens at 29.86 (VERIFIED) and the hand and watch are on the handle until about 31.9. 4:5 at 0.55 is fine.
7703 32.2-34.2, 35.2-37.2 and 53.6-57.3 all match inventory windows. The trickle stops before the chute empties at 37.7. VERIFIED.
scores.note: Cutting on the camera's own moves inside one take reads as a single event. The dark band is justified because it sits on the roasting copy. Shot math checks: 2+2.2+2+2+3.7 minus 4 dissolves is about 10.6 s. It overlaps concept 23 (same footage, same page), so choose this one if the tray loop is wanted. Note that Home (concept 1) also quotes the drop.

scores.name: FAQ: the bloom inside the roast-date answer
clip_errors: 7052 2.0-7.9 is the inventory's clean window (jerk max 0.168). First contact at about 2.1 and bubbles at about 3.2 are VERIFIED.
4:5 at 0.48 (0.255-0.705) drops the kettle bar. Red-channel clipping on the sunlit filter wall (9-11%) may fall inside the crop.
scores.note: The footage is clean and the cost is low (~1.5 MB, loaded on demand). But no SNöBI bag is in frame, the coffee is UNKNOWN, and a bloom only implies freshness indirectly. It is low-impact proof hidden in an accordion. Fine as a later polish item.

scores.name: Trade: one espresso stream beside the inquiry
rule_violations: Nothing proves the beans in the cup are SNöBI, and the venue is INFERRED. Concept 15 excludes these same espresso clips for exactly this reason, so the two Trade concepts contradict each other.
clip_errors: The claim that the loop 'starts after the 33.7-34.8 sway peak' is wrong. 34.03 is inside the 33.7-34.8 sway, so the first ~0.8 s of the loop carries it. Start at about 34.8, or accept the sway in the crossfade.
The loop endpoint diff of 10.9 and the 4:5 crop at 0.44 are VERIFIED. The steady sub-window runs 32.0-38.6.
scores.note: Technically clean and cheap, but it sells someone's espresso rather than SNöBI's organic beans. Concept 15 serves /trade better with real bags and the roastery chain.

scores.name: Cart: the drum window next to the roast-day line
rule_violations: The concept bundles a registry change (computing nextRoastDay with a cutoff and JP holidays). That change is good, but the effort is far above S.
clip_errors: 7596 0.2-3.2 is the inventory loop (endpoints within about 4/3 px). VERIFIED.

The beans are motion streaks most of the time. At 160 CSS px, a 330-380 px crop of the window will read as flickering dark noise, not as beans. The olive colour early in the roast reads as raw coffee.
scores.note: Motion at checkout plus a dark inset on a light panel gives little signal, and it competes with concept 10 for the same drawer. Keep the registry fix as its own task. The literal '火・金焙煎。焙煎日翌営業日に発送。' in cart.tsx is VERIFIED; derive that copy from the registry and drop the video.

scores.name: Journal: the first Roastery post, green to sealed
rule_violations: The dim figures (7290 at luma about 95, the tray at about 35) are acknowledged as a bend. This is acceptable inside an editorial post.
clip_errors: 7289 7.4-9.4 at 9:16 0.55 excludes the blue corner that returns at 7.2. VERIFIED.
7290 20.2-24.7: the first and last frames match, but the texture diff is about 12.5-14, so the crossfade must stay at 0.5 s or less. VERIFIED.
7703 45.1-48.9 includes the camera settle at 45.1-45.5 (2-4 px/frame), so a 45.5 in point would be cleaner.
7669 15.0-17.6: the bag's SNöBI identity is INFERRED and the label is upside down.
scores.note: The right home for footage that is true but too dim or too specialised for commerce pages, and the exclusion list is well reasoned. It depends on the Journal build and a video variant of Figure, so it is a later phase. Drop figure 5 unless the 7669 bag is confirmed as SNöBI.

scores.name: 焙煎日は袋に: the bag, opened (roast date and whole bean from one take)
rule_violations: Showing a legible Peru info label while 7208 (same lot) has a VERIFIED misregistered table and an all-zero barcode is a STOP condition until the 7209 label is checked.
A Peru-only specimen on all four origin pages misrepresents the Ethiopia, Mexico and Colombia pages.
clip_errors: Timeline contradiction: 1.0-3.5 at real speed reaches source 3.5 at t=2.5, then 'holds on the 2.8 s frame', which means jumping back 0.7 s. End the play at source 2.8 (t=1.8) or freeze on the last frame.
The label is readable only to about 3.4, and its centre drifts from x 0.48 to 0.62. A fixed 0.55 crop holds until about 3.5 only.
16.05-17.65 is VERIFIED: sharp, the best loop (diff 8.22), crop 0.55. The near hand covers 30-40% of the crop at lower right.
scores.note: Strong idea: a live computed date next to a printed specimen. The weekday math is plausible (2026/09/22 is a Tuesday). But the evidence base is a possibly non-compliant label shot against dark green sacks (luma 75-107). Effort M ignores a possible reprint and reshoot. Do the label check first.

scores.name: The plate fills to free shipping (add-to-cart moment)
rule_violations: Runs at real speed instead of 50% (ghosting is VERIFIED). This is a documented bend.
Generic styled bean-on-plate footage with no SNöBI identity. Concept 1 and concept 8 reject this exact plate set as brand-neutral.
clip_errors: 7251 timeline mapping VERIFIED: first bean 3.83 (0.83 film), trickle 4.45-4.9, main stream 5.1-7.2, lull 7.2-7.6, second wave 7.65-9.0, settled 9.35. The 1:1 window at 0.47 (0.189-0.751) holds the heart (0.22-0.70) and the stream.
3.0-3.83 sits in a segment with every second's jerk above 0.30 (0.403-0.572), so stabilising it is mandatory.
Prices VERIFIED in content/products.ts: every 100 g bag is under ¥3,000 and Peru 200 g is ¥4,720. The threshold is a literal 3000 in shipping-progress.tsx (VERIFIED).
scores.note: A clever binding of real footage to cart state, using the clip's own lull as the stop point, and the code computes the state (good under TYPED_JUDGMENTS). But it is gimmick-adjacent, it plays at checkout, and it fights concept 7 for the drawer. A/B test it. Effort is S to M once the threshold moves into the registry.

scores.name: Read the bag: four claims, four printed lines
rule_violations: Using the 製造者 address to stand for 'roasted in Tokyo' is an inference, not a printed claim.
A label annotation diagram is close in spirit to the banned 'we show our work' line, and it puts a magnifier on a label that may be non-compliant.
clip_errors: 6572 8.55-10.0: per-second jerk is 0.342 at s8, and the segment also swings luma from 112 to 167 (peak 10.3) as the bag enters the sun. The freeze frame at 10.0 is close to that peak, so the label text may clip.
At 10 s the bag plus strip spans 0.17-0.88. The mobile 4:5 crop at 0.5 cuts the strip; the inventory gives crop null for this segment.
The table order and barcode on the Ethiopia label are UNKNOWN. The fallback stills at 4.0 and 4.5 are VERIFIED to show half the label each.
scores.note: High risk with weak support: the label compliance is unverified, the frame is the brightest and least steady in the clip, the dated label ages, and one claim is inferred. If the label is reprinted, reshoot one clean still instead.

scores.name: The lineup builds (Coffee page header)
clip_errors: The 6586 windows 10.0-11.1, 12.45-13.35, 14.9-15.7 and 19.02-22.22 all sit inside the hand-free beats. VERIFIED. 14.9 is right at the edge (a hand is at the top right at 14.8).
The timeline sums shot lengths without subtracting dissolve overlap, so the real film is about 7.6 s, not 8.6 s. The median shot is still within the band.
The final loop at 50% is 6.4 s. Each beat sits on a different framing (up to 6.5 deg of roll and 100 px), so the 10-20% crop-in is an estimate.
scores.note: This is the same concept as concept 2, minus the empty-table plate. It is simpler, with no speck patch or plate offset. Build exactly one of concepts 2, 12 and 22. This one is the lower-risk variant.

scores.name: Same sun: the real bag after the 3D bag
clip_errors: 6572 1.17-2.07 is the inventory's only clean ping-pong range. VERIFIED. 4:5 at 0.45 leaves about 0.025 margin per side. The green watch band at lower right may stay in frame.
6586 9.8-11.1 for Peru: there is a fingertip at 9.6 and the next bag at 11.25, so the window is valid. The drift of 0.07 and the luma climb from 124 to 136 mean it plays once only. Correctly stated.
Mexico's centre of about 0.75 in the final hold is INFERRED, not measured. The inventory confirms MEXICO is readable but does not list DECAF for the final hold.
scores.note: Answers the user's 'other photos of each bag' question most directly: the real bag in daylight next to the buy card. Fold concept 3's live roast-date stamp into this one. The Colombia and Mexico pages sharing one frame is a known compromise; a short single-bag reshoot on the 6572 desk would fix it.

scores.name: Decaf in the low sun (Mexico page brew pair)
rule_violations: The HARIO wordmark is in the close-up for the whole sharp window and needs masking.
clip_errors: 7074 10.15-11.4: fingertips stay at the top-left until about 12.2. Whether a 1.05x punch-in clears them is INFERRED. Concept 3 uses 1.08x for the same problem.
7074 17.6-18.9 is inside the sharp window 17.4-20.9. VERIFIED. The pouch label is cut off in the close-up (MEXICO/DECAF never in frame).
scores.note: Honest attribution, because the pouch is in the wide shot. But it overlaps concept 3's Mexico slot, the 'late in the day' framing is inferred, and the third-party mark needs retouching. Merge into the Mexico page as one slot, not two.

scores.name: Trade: the range at the counter, then the chain behind it
rule_violations: Calling the window tile (luma about 73) 'no dark footage' is a stretch, but acceptable at tile size.
clip_errors: 7111 18.8-21.72: the 1:1 crop at 0.67 holds the mug and the Ethiopia label. VERIFIED against the inventory.

scores.note: The best long-form use of the footage, with a truthful through-line (one morning, 4K and timestamps VERIFIED in the grade README) and every timecode checks. Effort L is honest, and it is gated by the 4K conform, fonts in the renderer, licensed music and the 7669 decision. Do it after the site pieces.
